# Intake brief — Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results

## Problem statement

Returning to the hex map after a hex deployment currently reduces the whole
sortie to a single thin line (`RUN: VICTORY · score 1200`) plus a banked
win-bonus line, and on defeat it shows only `RUN: DEFEAT` with no explanation of
why the hex was not taken. The player cannot see, in one place, what the battle
outcome was, which rewards (salvage, granted weapon/upgrade, special reward,
contract/cache bonus) were actually paid, or — on a loss — what the defending
boss was strong and weak against. This brief adds a **post-battle results
dialog** on the hex map that presents that detail.

## Users

The **player** finishing a hex deployment in the Hangar War outer loop, and the
**attract/demo traversal** that must not stall on the new surface.

- As a player who won a hex, I want a dialog that tells me the outcome, my
  score and every reward I received, so I know exactly what the sortie earned me.
- As a player who lost a hex, I want a dialog that summarises the enemy boss's
  strengths and weaknesses (and the reward I missed), so I can plan the retake.
- As a player or watcher, I want to dismiss the dialog with one input (and have
  the attract demo auto-dismiss it) so the map stays playable and never stalls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a hex deployment ends, landing on `HexMapScene` presents a modal dialog over the paused map stating the battle outcome (`VICTORY`/`DEFEAT`) and the run's final score.
- On victory the dialog itemises every reward that was actually paid — salvage banked (minerals/cores), any granted weapon/upgrade, any special-mission reward, any contract and/or cache bonus, and the banked win bonus — and shows no line for a reward that was not paid.
- On defeat the dialog summarises the target hex boss's authored strengths and weaknesses (from `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`) and states the grant the player did not claim; it also states the unbanked salvage that was forfeited.
- The dialog is dismissible by a single confirm input (keyboard or pointer); dismissal resumes the map, and in demo/attract mode the dialog auto-dismisses after the shared dwell so the traversal cannot stall on it.
- The dialog's contents are produced by a shared, pure "result for view" builder over the game's own capture/defeat record and the authored hex definition (the dialog derives no reward or weakness itself), covered by unit tests plus a landing integration test that boots `HexMapScene` with a sortie result and asserts the dialog text and dismissal.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

After every hex battle the player gets one clear results dialog that names the
outcome, the rewards actually earned and, on a loss, the enemy's strengths and
weaknesses — so no sortie ends on a bare `RUN: DEFEAT` line with no explanation.

## Constraints

- **Reuse the shipped overlay pattern.** The map already pauses itself at the
  `SceneManager` level and launches `MiniBossWheelScene` / `MineralChoiceScene`
  over the paused map. The results dialog follows the same single-overlay
  contract (launch → pause → optional `onResult` callback → resume), including
  the demo auto-resolve rule (`HexMapScene.presentReward`).
- **One rule, no re-derivation.** Reward figures come from the capture cycle's
  own `HexCaptureResult` (`resolveHexCapture`) and the defeat path's
  `resolveDeploymentDefeat`; the boss strengths/weaknesses come from the authored
  hex definition. The dialog/view model must never re-derive a number.
- **Transient launch data only.** Like the existing run line, win bonus and
  assault banner, the sortie result is never persisted; a later menu/hangar
  re-entry shows no dialog.
- **Gym parity note.** `GymHexWar` is a read-only ring harness that runs no
  deployment and no combat, so it cannot show a post-battle dialog; this is a
  landing-surface presentation of the game's finished deployment, not a gameplay
  object, and needs no divergent gym copy.

## Risks

- **Handoff drift.** The reward detail lives in `HexCaptureResult`, not in the
  map today; if the handoff copies fields by hand, a new reward kind could be
  silently dropped from the dialog. Mitigation: pass the shipped record and let
  the pure builder read it, so a new reward field surfaces without a second edit.
- **Duplicated presentation.** If the dialog is added but the thin run line and
  win-bonus line are left in place, the landing shows the same facts twice.
  Mitigation: assumption A1 folds them in; a test asserts the dialog carries the
  outcome/score/win bonus.
- **Demo stall.** A modal that waits for input would freeze the attract
  traversal. Mitigation: reuse the existing demo auto-resolve rule so the dialog
  auto-dismisses after the shared dwell (asserted in a test).
- **Scope creep.** Related opportunities (e.g. surfacing the defeating bot's
  skills, or a full sortie history) are recorded as separate linked items rather
  than folded into this brief.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene` ends a hex deployment by starting `HexMapScene` with
  `{ payload, record, won, score, reward, assault, winBonusMinerals, demo,
  demoDwellMs }` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, the `_endRun` hangar-war branch).
- `HexMapScene` renders the map and a thin `runLine()`
  (`RUN: VICTORY|DEFEAT · score N`) plus the model's `winBonusLine` and, when a
  ring-end assault fired, the `RING WON` / `HANGAR FALLS` banner. It presents the
  mini-boss reward over the paused map via `presentReward()`.
- `HexCaptureResult` (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`) already carries every
  reward number a victory paid: `bankedDelta`, `grant`, `specialReward`,
  `contractBonus`, `cachePayout`, `defender`, `ringSecured`, `ringAdvanced`,
  `assault`. The defeat path `resolveDeploymentDefeat` yields the `forfeited`
  salvage. **None of this is currently handed to the map** — only `assault`,
  `won`, `score` and `winBonusMinerals` are.
- Boss intel is authored per hex in `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`
  (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`): `boss`, `strengths`, `weaknesses`,
  `grants`, and is already surfaced in the map's detail panel.

## Desired change

1. Extend the deployment→map handoff so `HexMapScene` receives a compact
   **sortie result** for the finished deployment: the target hex id, the
   capture result's reward fields (`bankedDelta`, `grant`, `specialReward`,
   `contractBonus`, `cachePayout`, `ringSecured`, `ringAdvanced`) on a win, and
   `forfeited` on a loss (plus `won`/`score`/`winBonusMinerals`, already there).
2. Add a pure **results-for-view builder** (e.g.
   `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts`) that turns that record plus the authored
   hex definition into ordered dialog rows: outcome + score, every paid reward,
   and — only on defeat — the boss's strengths/weaknesses and the unclaimed
   grant. No rule lives in the scene.
3. Add the **results dialog overlay** (a new scene mirroring
   `MineralChoiceScene`'s pause/launch contract, or a modal section of the
   shared `hexMap` renderer) and present it on `HexMapScene.create()` when a
   sortie result is carried, before the demo dwell starts. A single confirm
   input dismisses it; demo auto-dismisses after the shared dwell.
4. Fold the now-redundant thin `runLine()` / win-bonus announcement into the
   dialog on a deployment landing (assumption A1), leaving the distinct
   hangar-assault banner in place.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — add the sortie result (capture/defeat record + target hex id) to the `scene.start(HEX_MAP_SCENE_KEY, …)` handoff at run end.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — accept, hold and present the sortie result; fold the thin run line into the dialog; resume the map on dismissal (and demo dwell).
- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts` (new, or extend `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) — pure results-for-view builder consuming the record + `HexRingDefinition`; the single source of dialog text.
- `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.ts` (new, or a modal section in `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`) — the pause/launch overlay with a single confirm dismissal, mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` / `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — types already carried (`HexCaptureResult`, `DeploymentDefeatResult`, `SalvageAmounts`); no rule change expected.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — authored `strengths`/`weaknesses`/`grants` read by the builder (no change expected).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.test.ts` (new) — coverage for the builder and the landing dialog.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D § UI / scene surface) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — record the new landing surface and the gym-parity note.

## Related work

- `AH-0MWEXIOZZ009UX14` — Scene: `HexMapScene` accepts record/run-line/reward and presents the reward over the paused map.
- `AH-0MWEZZA4E0081NJ5` — Assault defence report and reset announcement.
- `AH-0MWF2Q2JC008MAJE` — DefenceReportScene: announce the banked win bonus before the map.
- `AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP` — Between-sortie frontier tick and the deployment→map landing handoff.
- `AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6` — Capture cycle, hex boss variant and defending bot.
- `AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2` — Hex map scene.
- `AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS` — Reduce length of hexmap battles.
- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, § *UI / scene surface* and § *Known-ahead intel and anti-checklist mitigations*.

## Appendix: Assumptions and questions for producer confirmation

These are repo-grounded assumptions made to keep intake moving; the producer
may override any of them at review. No question was answered interactively
during this intake pass.

- **A1 — Dialog replaces the thin map lines.** The results dialog carries the
  outcome, score and win bonus that the current `runLine()` and `winBonusLine`
  show, so those two are folded into the dialog on a deployment landing to
  avoid duplication. The `RING WON` / `HANGAR FALLS` hangar-assault banner stays
  as a separate, distinct announcement. *If the producer prefers the dialog to
  appear alongside the existing lines, this is a presentation-only change and
  does not affect the ACs.*
- **A2 — "Enemy strengths and weaknesses" means the target hex boss.** The
  summary uses the target hex's authored `strengths` / `weaknesses` in
  `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`, plus the `grant` the player did not claim. The
  defending-bot `skills` are not summarised unless the producer asks.
- **A3 — Blocking modal, one confirm to dismiss, demo auto-dismiss.** The
  dialog pauses the map (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`) and is dismissed by a
  single keyboard/pointer confirm; in demo/attract mode it auto-dismisses after
  the shared dwell so the traversal cannot stall.
- **A4 — Both outcomes show the dialog.** A victory shows outcome + rewards; a
  defeat shows outcome + the boss strengths/weaknesses + the unclaimed grant and
  the forfeited unbanked salvage.
- **A5 — Data must be extended, not re-derived.** The map currently receives no
  capture reward detail; the handoff must be extended to carry the capture
  cycle's own record rather than the map recomputing rewards.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB** – Held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES map action and wiring (blocked)
- **AH-0MWEXIOZZ009UX14** – Scene: HexMapScene accepts record/run-line/reward and presents the reward over the paused map (completed)
- **AH-0MWCOW6KA008OJOL** – Win-path reward after the defence report (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mwdcbvq700579ws, 0mwf2q2jc008maje, accept, acceptance, accepts (+347 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvuxcag90086lh2, accept, acceptance, accepts, actually (+334 more)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, accepts, actually, add (+283 more)


## Plan — feature decomposition (plan skill, 2026-11-18)

Decomposed into **7 children** in test-first dependency order. Each child is a
minimal end-to-end slice (code + tests + the docs/observability its layer owns);
the contract is pinned by tests before the implementation items land, in the
repo's red-before/green-after convention.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|------------|
| 1 | TEST-FIRST: pin the sortie results dialog contract (`AH-0MWMGPPIR009DOKR`) | task | — |
| 2 | Pure sortie result view builder (`AH-0MWMGPQUE0064AFH`) | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Deployment handoff carries the sortie result (`AH-0MWMGPS9R008SMEG`) | feature | 2 |
| 4 | Hex combat result dialog overlay scene (`AH-0MWMGPTNF004EX3T`) | feature | 2 |
| 5 | `HexMapScene` presents the results dialog on landing (`AH-0MWMGPV420013MGB`) | feature | 3, 4 |
| 6 | Docs: record the hex combat results dialog (`AH-0MWMGPWJM00181ST`) | docs | 5 |
| 7 | Sortie results dialog end-to-end verification (`AH-0MWMGPY2U009XMBD`) | task | 5, 6 |

### Vertical-slice phasing

This is one landing-surface slice, not a multi-phase epic, so there are no
phase gates. Where the plan does split work it splits on **module boundaries**
that are independently shippable — the pure builder (2) and the overlay scene
(4) both run in isolation, and 3 and 4 can land in either order before the map
wiring (5) joins them. Every child still cuts through its own layers: a pure
model plus unit tests (2), a scene plus its registry and capture entries (4), a
handoff plus its launch-data test (3), a landing plus its stepped-frame
integration test (5), and the documentation of record (6).

**Between children:** re-read the next child's description before starting it
and update it if the shipped shape has moved (for example the exact
`SortieResultRecord` field names fixed by child 2, which children 3–5 quote from
the intake rather than from code).

### Design decisions recorded by this plan

- **A dedicated overlay scene, not a modal section of the shared renderer.**
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` is rendered by both the game's `HexMapScene`
  and the read-only `GymHexWar`. A blocking modal inside the shared renderer
  would force every gym render to make a modal/parity decision, while the
  intake records that `GymHexWar` runs no deployment and can never land. A
  separate `HexCombatResultScene` (child 4) mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s
  launch/pause/callback contract keeps the shared renderer untouched and the
  gym divergence-free, and matches the shipped overlay pattern the constraint
  section names.
- **Carry the shipped records, not a copied subset.** Child 3 hands the map the
  capture cycle's own `HexCaptureResult` and the defeat path's `forfeited`
  salvage, so the parent's "handoff drift" risk is closed by design: a reward
  field added to the capture cycle later reaches the dialog without a second
  copy edit.
- **Fold the thin lines (assumption A1), keep the assault banner.** Child 5
  drops the deployment `RUN:` line and the `WIN BONUS BANKED:` line from the
  landing render and carries both facts in the dialog; the distinct
  `RING WON` / `HANGAR FALLS` assault banner is unchanged.

### Open questions for producer review (non-blocking — defaults taken)

- **OPEN QUESTION (A1, presentation):** on a deployment landing, does the
  results dialog *replace* the thin `RUN: VICTORY|DEFEAT · score N` line and the
  `WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS` line, or appear *alongside* them?
  **Recommended: replace** — the shared renderer already has a "transient news
  has one home" rule (`renderLastSortieSection`), and showing the same outcome
  and bonus twice on one screen reads as duplicated presentation.
  *Default taken by this plan: replace.* Direction to whom: producer. Why it
  matters: only the landing render changes, not the ACs, but changing it later
  touches the assertions of child 5.
- **OPEN QUESTION (A2, content):** on a defeat, does the dialog also summarise
  the defending bot's `skills` (as well as the authored boss
  strengths/weaknesses)?
  **Recommended: no** — the parent AC names the authored boss intel, and the
  intake records the defending bot as separate scope (scope-creep risk).
  *Default taken by this plan: no.* Direction to whom: producer. Why it
  matters: if yes, child 2 gains a second data source.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Recorded per the shared interview conduct contract. **Idempotent** — a re-run of
the plan skill updates these entries rather than adding new ones.

- **Q1: Is the plan blocked on the two remaining effort/risk unknowns (A1
  dialog replaces or sits alongside the thin lines; A2 whether the defeating
  bot's skills are summarised)?**
  Answer: no answer was given in-session — this planning run was
  downtime-dispatched by `herdr-downtime` and had no interactive producer to
  answer (session dispatch comment `AH-C0MWMGIK4N002H5NA`). The plan proceeds on
  the parent intake's recorded, repo-grounded defaults (A1 = replace,
  A2 = no) and records both above as OPEN QUESTIONs for producer review with a
  recommendation each. Evidence: this item's intake Appendix, A1/A2 entries;
  the effort/risk report's `unknowns` list (`AH-C0MWMG771R000KCLT`).
- **Q2: Which shipped records does the dialog read its figures from?**
  Answer (agent, repo evidence): the capture cycle's `HexCaptureResult`

# Pure sortie result view builder

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

The results dialog must present the sortie's outcome, its paid rewards and — on
a defeat — the target boss's strengths/weaknesses, without the scene deriving
any of it. Today the reward detail lives only in `HexCaptureResult`
(`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`) and the defeat detail in
`DeploymentDefeatResult`; the boss intel is authored per hex in
`HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`. This item adds the single pure module that turns those
records into ordered dialog rows, so the scene renders text it was handed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The dialog's contents are produced by a shared, pure "result for view" builder over the game's own capture/defeat record and the authored hex definition (the dialog derives no reward or weakness itself), covered by unit tests in this item plus the landing integration test in the `HexMapScene` child that boots `HexMapScene` with a sortie result and asserts the dialog text and dismissal.
- A new pure module `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts` defines the compact `SortieResultRecord` the map receives (won, score, target hex id, banked win bonus, the carried `HexCaptureResult` on a victory, the forfeited `SalvageAmounts` on a defeat) and `buildSortieResultView(record, definition)` returning ordered rows for the dialog.
- On a victory the rows are: outcome + score first, then salvage banked (minerals/cores), any granted weapon/upgrade, any special-mission reward, any contract bonus, any cache payout and the banked win bonus — each only when it was actually paid, never a zero line.
- On a defeat the rows are: outcome + score, the target hex's authored `strengths` and `weaknesses`, the grant the player did not claim, and the forfeited unbanked salvage.
- The builder **re-derives nothing**: every reward figure and every strength/weakness string is copied from the carried record or the authored `HexRingDefinition`; the module imports no Phaser, reads no store and mutates no input (a frozen input is not thrown on).
- A sortie result whose target hex is absent from the supplied definitions degrades to the outcome + score rows (and, on a victory, the carried reward rows) instead of throwing or inventing boss intel.
- Unit tests cover every reward kind present and absent for both outcomes, the forfeited-salvage line, the unknown-hex fallback and input immutability.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts` (new)
- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (types read only — `HexCaptureResult`, `DeploymentDefeatResult`; no rule change)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` (the `HexRingDefinition` shape)
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` (`SalvageAmounts`)

- Contract pinned first: TEST-FIRST sortie results dialog contract

# Deployment handoff carries the sortie result

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

At run end `PlayScene._finishRun` starts `HexMapScene` with
`{ payload, record, won, score, reward, assault, winBonusMinerals, demo,
demoDwellMs }`. The reward detail a victory paid (`HexCaptureResult`) and the
salvage a defeat forfeited (`DeploymentDefeatResult.forfeited`) never leave
`PlayScene`, so the map cannot show them. This item extends that handoff to
carry the compact sortie result the new builder consumes — passing the shipped
records, never a hand-copied subset of their numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PlayScene` resolves a `SortieResultRecord` at the end of a hex deployment (win: the target hex id from the hangar deployment plus the capture cycle's own `HexCaptureResult` from `resolveHexCapture`; loss: the target hex id plus the `forfeited` salvage `resolveDeploymentDefeat` settled) and adds it to the `scene.start(HEX_MAP_SCENE_KEY, …)` launch data.
- The handoff carries the shipped record objects rather than individually copied reward fields, so a reward kind added to `HexCaptureResult` later reaches the map without a second copy edit; no figure is recomputed on either side.
- `HexMapSceneData` gains the optional `sortie` field and `HexMapScene` holds it, exposes it through a `getSortieResult()` query seam returning a detached copy, and never persists it — no payload field, no store migration, and a later menu/hangar re-entry (which carries no `sortie`) shows no result.
- A defeat landing carries the forfeited unbanked salvage; a victory landing carries no `forfeited` value (nothing is forfeited on a win).
- Tests cover the victory handoff (capture record fields survive to the map), the defeat handoff (forfeited salvage survives), the detached-copy seam and the "launch data only" rule.

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (the `_finishRun` hangar-war branch and `_forfeitUnbankedSalvage`)

# Hex combat result dialog overlay scene

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

The map already presents the shipped mini-boss reward over a paused map through
`MiniBossWheelScene`/`MineralChoiceScene` (launch → pause → optional callback →
resume). The results dialog needs the same single-overlay contract but a
different body: read-only rows and one confirm to dismiss. This item adds that
overlay scene and registers it, so the landing child only has to launch it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new scene `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.ts` (key `HEX_COMBAT_RESULT_SCENE_KEY`) renders the ordered rows it is handed — a heading plus labelled lines — and derives no reward, score, weakness or rule of its own (no import of the capture cycle, the hex definitions or the store).

- In demo mode (`autoConfirmMs > 0`) it auto-confirms after that delay so the attract traversal cannot stall on it; normal play omits the delay and waits for the player.
- The scene is registered in the boot scene list (`src/core/gameConfig.ts`) and its capturability is decided explicitly in `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` with `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` updated to match, so the scene registry and the capture registry cannot drift.
- Tests cover: rows rendered verbatim, one confirm per dismissal (a second confirm cannot fire `onDismiss` twice), the keyboard and pointer paths, the demo auto-confirm delay, and the no-callback close.

# HexMapScene presents the results dialog on landing

Child of AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN (Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results).

## Problem statement

`HexMapScene.create()` builds the map and either presents a carried mini-boss
reward or schedules the demo dwell; the finished sortie is reduced to a thin
`runLine()` (`RUN: VICTORY|DEFEAT · score N`) plus the model's `winBonusLine`.
This item presents the carried sortie result as the results dialog over the
paused map before the demo dwell starts, and folds the two now-redundant lines
into it (parent assumption A1), leaving the distinct `RING WON` / `HANGAR FALLS`
assault banner in place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a hex deployment ends, landing on `HexMapScene` presents a modal dialog over the paused map stating the battle outcome (`VICTORY`/`DEFEAT`) and the run's final score.
- A landing that carries a sortie result presents the results dialog over the **paused** map, before the demo dwell is scheduled; the dialog text is the carried builder's rows (no scene-side derivation) and names the outcome (`VICTORY`/`DEFEAT`), the run's final score and every reward actually paid.
- A single confirm input dismisses the dialog, resumes the map and — in demo mode — restarts the shared dwell, so the attract traversal cannot stall on the dialog (a stepped-frame test advances from the landing through the dismissal to the next deployment).
- A landing with no sortie result (a plain menu/hangar re-entry) shows no dialog, and the sortie result is consumed exactly once so a second presentation path cannot re-show it.
- If the dialog overlay is not registered (headless test or misconfiguration) the map stays live and the demo dwell still starts, mirroring `presentReward()`'s no-stall rule.
- On a deployment landing the thin `runLine()` and the banked `winBonusLine` are no longer drawn — the dialog carries the outcome, score and win bonus — while the `assault` banner renders unchanged; the ordering with a carried mini-boss reward is deterministic and documented (sortie dialog first, then any reward).
- Tests cover both outcomes, the paused-map presentation, one-confirm dismissal and resume, the demo auto-dismiss without stall, the plain re-entry, the unregistered-overlay fallback and the folded-line assertions.

# Chime whenever a mineral is collected

## Problem statement

Collecting minerals — the game's core economy loop — is completely silent
today: `_collectMineral` credits the hold and updates the HUD bar, but the
player gets no audio confirmation at all. A successful mineral run therefore
feels flat, and the only confirmation is a small HUD bar the player is not
looking at during combat.

## Users

- **Player (game):** wants collecting minerals to feel rewarding and immediate
  without looking away from the ship.
  - *As a player, when my ship picks up a mineral I hear a quiet, satisfying
    chime so the pickup registers without me checking the HUD.*
  - *As a player, when I sweep up a scatter of minerals in quick succession
    the chime steps upward so a good run reads as rising musical momentum —
    and it settles back to its base note once I stop collecting.*
- **Maintainer / gym author:** needs the feedback to run the same code in the
  game and every gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity), with the pitch/level tuning
  in one place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every **player** mineral pickup plays a quiet chime: one chime per collected
  mineral, on every path that credits the mineral hold (`PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene` and its subclasses, `GymLevel`, `GymPowerUpsUtility` and
  the leveling gyms' mineral supply), through **one shared implementation** —
  no per-scene copy of the pitch/escalation logic.
- The chime **rises in pitch** with each successive pickup while the player
  keeps collecting, and **resets to its base pitch** after a gap of
  `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` (1.5 s) with no pickup; the rise is capped at a
  documented ceiling (A-minor ladder `[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]` semitones, i.e.
  up to one octave) so a long streak never becomes shrill.
- The chime is **subtle and quiet**: the baked asset peaks at ≤ 0.2 (the
  documented player-cue ceiling in GDD §7.3) with a stated target level in the
  recipe header, and it never masks enemy-fire telegraphs. It obeys the global
  SFX volume/mute settings and the shared per-cue voice limiter, and degrades
  to a silent no-op with no `AudioContext` (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
  browsers).
- **Enemy absorption plays no chime** — the feedback is player-only (an enemy
  hoovering up a mineral must not read as a player reward).
- New cue is delivered through the existing **ToneForge baked pipeline**: a new
  `aihell-mineral-chime` recipe (next free seed **32292**), a manifest entry, a
  deterministic baked WAV plus committed checksum, and `npm run
  build-audio:verify` passes unchanged for every pre-existing asset.
- The pitch-escalation state machine is **pure and unit-tested** with an
  injected clock: rise per pickup, cap, reset after the gap, and reset on
  run restart / scene teardown. A dense burst (several minerals in one frame,
  a 100-mineral gym field, Mineral Scoop sweep) is bounded — it may not
  shotgun-stack chimes beyond the shared voice limiter.
- Tests cover the cue (export + manifest + resolvable baked asset), the
  escalation state machine, and the shared wiring in the game and in the gyms.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (specifically
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` both tables and GDD §7.3 /
  §4.5).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Collecting minerals now rewards the ear as well as the HUD: each pickup gives a
quiet chime that steps upward through a quick scatter, so a mineral run feels
satisfying and audibly productive without the player ever glancing at the
mineral bar.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** the escalation rule and the cue dispatch live
  once; the game and every gym consume the same implementation. Divergence, if
  any (e.g. the leveling gyms' bespoke collection loops), must be justified in
  the work item and in a code comment.
- **Baked audio only:** no runtime synthesis. The cue must be a ToneForge
  recipe rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`, with SHA-256 checksums committed
  to `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`; renders are deterministic (the pipeline
  renders twice and compares).
- **Enemy-balance guards are untouched:** the new recipe is a *player* cue, so it
  is tagged `player`/`mineral`/`pickup` with no enemy tag and no
  `AMPLITUDE_TIERS` key (the guard only analyses the enemy family). The A-minor
  conformance guard likewise applies to enemy cues only, but the pitch ladder is
  musical anyway so the cue sits inside the game's tonal language.
- **Player-cue ceiling** ≤ 0.2 peak (GDD §7.3), and every existing player cue
  degrades to a silent no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- **No second throttle:** the shared per-cue voice limiter (4 voices / 150 ms,
  `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts`) already bounds overlap through the one
  `playCue` funnel; add no parallel rate limiter.
- **Reset gap is game time, not wall time**, so a paused scene cannot expire a
  streak mid-run and the streak does not depend on frame rate.
- **Purely audio:** no change to mineral economy, drop rules, collection
  geometry, scoring, telemetry or the hold model.
- No new persisted `rules.ts` tunable — pitch/level/length are fixed named
  constants beside the cue (precedent: `COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES`,
  `WAVE_LASER_VOLUME_SCALE`), so retuning is a one-line change with no re-bake.
- Scope-creep guard: extra opportunities found on the way (e.g. a pitch ladder
  for power-up pickups, a streak HUD indicator) are recorded as separate linked
  work items, not folded into this one.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "slightly" means small steps — one A-minor scale degree per
  pickup, capped at an octave. If the producer prefers a chromatic ladder or a
  smaller cap, only `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES` changes.
- **Assumption:** the reset window is 1.5 s (`MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS`), the
  "short period" in the brief; one constant to retune.
- **Assumption:** a red 10-value deposit and a scattered pair each chime once
  per collected mineral, not once per mineral *unit*, so a deposit does not fire
  ten chimes.
- **Risk — aliasing:** reusing `aihell-mineral-tinkle` (the Mystery UFO spill
  cue) would make a pickup indistinguishable from a spill; mitigated by a
  dedicated `aihell-mineral-chime` recipe.
- **Risk — audio clutter:** mineral fields are dense (gyms seed 100 minerals,
  Mineral Scoop sweeps, doubled drops). Mitigated by the voice limiter, a quiet
  baked level and the cap on the pitch ladder; verified by a dense-burst test.
- **Risk — pitch/duration coupling:** raising pitch via `playbackRate` also
  shortens the cue (0.2 s → 0.1 s at the octave). Accepted (the countdown tick
  precedent) and documented in the recipe comment.
- **Risk — render environment:** baking needs the local ToneForge CLI
  (`../ToneForge`); if it is unavailable the implementer must not hand-write a
  WAV — stop and report the blocker.

## Existing state

- Collection seam: `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` (`collectMinerals`) is
  shared by `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility`; each scene supplies an `onPlayerCollected` callback
  (`_collectMineral` / `_collectGymMineral`) that credits the hold and syncs the
  HUD. `GymWeaponLeveling` / `GymPowerUpLeveling` run their own bespoke
  overlap loops over a seeded mineral supply.
- No pickup sound exists anywhere on those paths.
- `playMineralTinkleSound()` (`aihell-mineral-tinkle`, seed 32290) exists but is
  the Mystery UFO **spill** cue, fired once per spill with the scattered drops.
- Pitch escalation by playback rate already ships for the countdown tick:
  `playCountdownTickSound(step)` + `COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES` +
  `countdownTickRate(step)` (`src/audio/effects.ts`).
- One cue funnel: `playCue()` applies the per-cue voice limiter, seed variant
  pick and the shared master gain; `SfxPlayOptions` supports `rate`, `volume`,
  `delay`, `loop`.
- The seed block 32100–32299 is reserved for game recipes; the highest shipped
  seed is 32291, so **32292** is the next free seed.
- Contract tests (`src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`,
  `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`) fail if an `effects.ts` cue has no
  manifest entry or no baked asset — a new cue cannot ship half-wired.

## Desired change

1. **New baked cue** `aihell-mineral-chime` — a short (~0.2 s, ≤ 0.2 peak)
   bright chime: one triangle/sine partial with a gentle decay and a quiet
   shimmer, deliberately distinct from `aihell-mineral-tinkle` (no falling
   E7 → A6 sweep, no noise tick) so a pickup never reads as a spill. Recipe,
   manifest entry (seed 32292), baked WAV, checksum.
2. **`playMineralCollectChimeSound()`** in `src/audio/effects.ts` — plays the
   cue at the current streak step's rate, with the semitone ladder, cap and gap
   as named constants.
3. **Shared escalation state machine** — a small Phaser-free module (e.g.
   `src/audio/mineralChime.ts`) owning the streak counter, the game-clock gap
   check and the reset, with an injectable clock for deterministic tests. One
   exported `noteMineralCollected(nowMs)` that advances the step and returns the
   playback rate, plus a reset seam for run restart / scene teardown.
4. **Wiring** — every player-collection path calls the shared seam exactly once
   per collected mineral (preferably from the shared collection layer or one
   shared core hook rather than five copies).
5. **Docs** — recipe header, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (mapping
   table + new-recipes table), GDD §7.3 cue table and the §4.5 collection
   bullet, plus the code comments recording the pitch-ladder and gap rationale.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` — New shared escalation state machine
  (streak step, cap, 1.5 s game-clock gap, reset seam; injectable clock).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — New `playMineralCollectChimeSound()` plus the
  semitone-ladder/gap constants beside the cue.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — Shared collection seam; preferred single
  dispatch point for the player-pickup chime.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_collectMineral` (game path; must not duplicate
  the escalation logic).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_collectMineral` (every
  formation gym).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  — Remaining player-collection paths / bespoke mineral loops.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Candidate shared hook if the dispatch
  belongs on the scene core instead of the collection layer.
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-mineral-chime.yaml` — New recipe (seed
  32292; document the level target and the rate/aliasing rationale).
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — New cue entry.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-mineral-chime.32292.wav`,
  `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — Baked asset + checksum
  (`npm run build-audio`).
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`
  (§7.3 cue table, §4.5 collection bullet) — Documentation rows/rationale.
- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` (new), `src/audio/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`, `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Coverage for the state
  machine, cue wiring and the defined-once/parity guards.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-19)

Decomposed into six child items, **test-first and dependency-ordered**. Each
child carries its own acceptance criteria, minimal implementation slice and
key files; this block is the traceability index only.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|-----------|
| 1 | Mineral chime escalation spec tests (AH-0MWNMRBO4000T5F8) | task | — |
| 2 | Pure mineral chime escalation state machine (AH-0MWNMRCEW006N0EH) | task | 1 |
| 3 | Baked aihell-mineral-chime cue (AH-0MWNMRD6I002CCVT) | task | 2 |
| 4 | One shared chime dispatch on every player pickup (AH-0MWNMRDY60005Z4K) | feature | 2, 3 |
| 5 | Document the mineral pickup chime (AH-0MWNMRER0009385Y) | docs | 4 |
| 6 | Verify the mineral chime end to end (AH-0MWNMRFJ9004F66R) | task | 4, 5 |

**Phase plan — each phase is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs/infra):**

1. **Pitch rule** (items 1→2): the pure state machine and the spec that drives
   it — behaviour, unit tests and documented constants land together.
2. **Audible cue** (item 3): recipe → deterministic bake → committed WAV +
   checksum → manifest entry → `effects.ts` export → contract and peak tests.
3. **Gameplay wiring** (item 4): the single shared core dispatch plus the six
   collection paths and the run-reset/teardown resets, with the parity,
   absorption-silence, defined-once and dense-burst tests.
4. **Docs** (item 5): cue-mapping tables, GDD §7.3/§4.5, README, code comments,
   pinned by a docs assertion test.
5. **Verification gate** (item 6): `build-audio:verify`, the full suite via the
   test skill, the production build and the ear check.

**Between phases:** re-read the next child's description and update it with
anything the previous slice learned (final constant names, cue name, test seams
to extend) before starting it. The children are the implementable
specification; this item's ACs are the coverage map.

**Architecture decision (recorded, no producer input needed):** the single
dispatch point is a shared `CombatCoreScene` hook, **not** the Phaser-free
`mineralLayer.collectMinerals`. Rationale, consequences and the parity argument
are in the wiring child's "Architecture decision" section.

**Plan changelog:** 2026-11-19 — first decomposition: 6 children created (issue
types task/task/task/feature/docs/task), 7 dependency edges wired, six automated
review stages run, AC coverage review = `proceed`. No prior plan block existed.

## Related work

- **Mystery UFO feel layer** (AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6) and its cue bake
  (AH-0MVSAJMLL00835T8) — shipped `aihell-mineral-tinkle` for the UFO **spill**,
  the closest existing mineral audio and the reason a pickup cue must not alias
  it.
- **Countdown count SFX cue via the ToneForge pipeline** (AH-0MV55OA93008OUL1)
  — the precedent for rising pitch through playback `rate` (`COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES`,
  `countdownTickRate`) and for adding a recipe/manifest/checksum/docs in one
  change.
- **Wire non-combat pickup audio into `GymPowerUps._collectDrop()`**
  (AH-0MTGS94T9007TAAC), **PlayScene: add per-type power-up pickup activation
  audio** (AH-0MU8QVX9G008P8ML) and **Pop SFX** (AH-0MUBYSNGU0051XVO) — the
  established pickup-feedback convention this item extends to minerals.
- **Mineral collectable entity and constants** (AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT), **Shared
  mineral layer** (AH-0MUII3DHM008L7JF) and **Red mineral deposits**
  (AH-0MVJ79739008396I) — the collection/value semantics the chime must not
  change (a deposit pays one chime, one 10-value pickup).
- **SFX mix** (AH-0MVZVMZOQ00076QF) — the family-trim mechanism
  (`*_VOLUME_SCALE` named constants) that a quieter chime should follow rather
  than re-baking assets.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake ran from an **automated downtime dispatch** (no interactive producer
present), so the three feel-tuning choices below could not be answered in
session. Each records the **recommended option** that the brief has adopted as
its documented default, the evidence behind it, and an **OPEN QUESTION** marker
so the producer can override any of them without re-planning (each is a single
named constant / one-line recipe change).

- **Q1 — Pitch ladder and ceiling:** how far should the chime rise, and in what
  steps? (a) chromatic, +1 semitone per pickup, capped at +7; (b) one **A-minor
  scale degree** per pickup, capped at an octave; (c) +2 semitones per pickup.
  **Recommended: (b)** — the game's written tonal language is A minor (GDD §7.3
  A-minor conformance, docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md), and one scale step reads
  as "slightly" rising without going shrill on a long streak. **OPEN QUESTION
  (provisional default: b; `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]`).**
  Source: no interactive answer — auto-dispatched intake; precedent evidence:
  `playCountdownTickSound` / `COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES` (AH-0MV55OA93008OUL1) in
  `src/audio/effects.ts`.
- **Q2 — Reset gap ("a short period"):** how long without a pickup before the
  pitch returns to base? (a) 1.0 s; (b) 1.5 s; (c) 2.0 s. **Recommended: (b)** —
  long enough to bridge sweeping a scattered pair (≈0.3–0.8 s apart) and short
  enough that a fresh pass starts clean. **OPEN QUESTION (provisional default:
  b; `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS = 1500`, measured on game time).** Source: no
  interactive answer — auto-dispatched intake.
- **Q3 — Cue identity:** add a dedicated baked recipe or reuse the existing
  `aihell-mineral-tinkle` at a rising rate? (a) new `aihell-mineral-chime`
  recipe (seed 32292); (b) reuse `aihell-mineral-tinkle`. **Recommended: (a)** —
  the existing tinkle is the Mystery UFO **spill** cue and fires at the moment
  the spilled minerals appear, so reusing it would make a pickup
  indistinguishable from a spill. Reuse also would not let the pickup be
  gain-staged independently. **OPEN QUESTION (provisional default: a).**
  Evidence: `playMineralTinkleSound` + GDD §4.5 / `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
  row for `aihell-mineral-tinkle`; no suitable unused pickup chime exists in the
  manifest (checked `playPowerUpCollectPopSound`, `playPowerUpCollectSound` —
  both are power-up-specific).
- **Q4 — Granularity:** does a red 10-value deposit (or a pair collected in one
  frame) chime once or ten/twice? **Decided by reading the brief**: one chime
  per *collected mineral entity* (so a deposit is one chime, a pair is two
  rising chimes), and enemy absorption is silent — the request is about the
  player collecting. Recorded here for traceability; producer may override.

**Duplicate-work check:** `wl search` for `mineral`, `tinkle`, `chime`,
`collect sound` and `audio cue` returned no open or completed item covering a
mineral-pickup chime; the closest is the Mystery UFO feel layer, which
**deliberately** voices only the spill. Comment recorded on the work item.

### Plan-session note (2026-11-19, automated dispatch)

The plan session also ran with no interactive producer, so no new questions were

# Mineral chime escalation spec tests

Part of **Chime whenever a mineral is collected** (AH-0MWNHEIV90047V91) — the
test-first slice for the pure pitch-escalation state machine. These tests are
written before the module exists (red) so the machine's behaviour is pinned
independently of any scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` exists and covers, driving the machine with
  an **injected clock only** (no wall clock, no Phaser, no audio mocking):
  - the first pickup sounds the **base** step (0 semitones → playback rate
    1.0);
  - each further pickup inside `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` advances exactly
    one ladder degree up `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES` (`[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]`);
  - a long streak **clamps** at the last ladder degree — it never exceeds one
    octave and never returns `undefined`/`NaN`/a negative rate for any
    non-negative pickup count;
  - a gap of exactly `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` resets to base, and a gap
    1 ms shorter does not (the boundary is pinned in both directions);
  - the explicit reset seam returns the streak to base;
  - two sequential streaks after a reset are independent (no shared/leaked
    state).
- Expected rates are computed as `2 ** (semitones / 12)` from the exported
  ladder, so the ladder (not a copy of its numbers) is the contract.
- The spec imports only the pure module — no `playCue` spy, no scene import.
- The cases fail before the implementation exists and pass afterwards with no
  weakening of their assertions (red → green).
- The pitch-escalation state machine is pure and unit-tested with an injected clock: rise per pickup, cap, reset after the gap, and reset on run restart / scene teardown; a dense burst is bounded and does not shotgun-stack chimes beyond the shared voice limiter (this item pins the pure part — the run-restart/teardown reset and the dense-burst bound are asserted by the wiring item).

## Minimal implementation

1. Create `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts`, one `describe` per rule above.
2. Hold a mutable `clock` variable in the test and pass it to every call —
   never `Date.now()`.
3. Keep the file Phaser-free.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` — new spec (the module does not exist yet).

## Dependencies

Blocks **Pure mineral chime escalation state machine** (test-first).

# Pure mineral chime escalation state machine

Part of **Chime whenever a mineral is collected** (AH-0MWNHEIV90047V91). Owns
the streak counter, the reset-gap check and the pitch ladder **once**, in a
Phaser-free module with an injected clock, so the game and every gym share the
rule and the tuning lives in one place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` exists and exports:
  - `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES` — the A-minor ladder `[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]`,
    documented as "one scale degree per pickup, capped at one octave";
  - `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` — `1500`, documented as **game time** (scene
    clock), not wall time;
  - `mineralChimeRate(step)` — `2 ** (semitones / 12)` for a clamped step
    (precedent: `countdownTickRate` in `src/audio/effects.ts`);
  - `noteMineralCollected(nowMs)` — advances the streak (or restarts it when
    the gap expired) and returns the **playback rate** to play;
  - `resetMineralChimeStreak()` — the run-restart / scene-teardown seam;
  - `mineralChimeStep()` — current step, for observability and tests.
- The module imports nothing from `scenes/`, `Phaser`, or `audio/effects`, and
  reads no wall clock (`Date.now`/`performance.now`); every time value comes
  from the caller.
- Behaviour matches the sibling spec item exactly (all its cases green).
- The module records, in comments, why the ladder is A-minor scale degrees,
  why the cap is an octave, and why the gap is game time (a paused scene must
  not expire a streak mid-run).
- No new persisted `rules.ts` tunable is introduced (fixed named constants).
- The chime rises in pitch with each successive pickup while the player keeps collecting, and resets to its base pitch after a gap of `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` (1.5 s) with no pickup; the rise is capped at a documented ceiling (A-minor ladder `[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]` semitones, up to one octave) so a long streak never becomes shrill.

## Minimal implementation

1. Module-local `step` and `lastPickupMs` state (module-scoped singleton, as
   `cueVoiceLimiter` does) plus a `createMineralChime()` factory for isolated
   instances in tests.
2. Clamp the step to `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES.length - 1`.
3. Reset when `nowMs - lastPickupMs > MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` — new module.
- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` — the spec it must satisfy.

## Dependencies

Depends on **Mineral chime escalation spec tests** (test-first). Blocks the cue
and the wiring items.

# Baked aihell-mineral-chime cue

Part of **Chime whenever a mineral is collected** (AH-0MWNHEIV90047V91). Adds
the new baked ToneForge cue and its playback wrapper — the audible half of the
feature — as one end-to-end slice: recipe → deterministic render → committed
asset + checksum → manifest entry → `effects.ts` export → contract tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-mineral-chime.yaml` exists with seed
  **32292** (the next free seed in the reserved 32100–32299 game block), tags
  `mineral`, `pickup`, `player` (no enemy tag) and `duration` ≈ 0.2 s. Its
  header documents the target peak level, the `playbackRate` pitch rise and
  the resulting duration shortening, and states how it is deliberately
  distinguishable from `aihell-mineral-tinkle` (no falling E7 → A6 sweep, no
  noise tick) so a pickup never reads as a UFO spill.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` carries one new baked entry pairing
  `playMineralCollectChimeSound` with `aihell-mineral-chime` and seed 32292;
  no existing entry changes.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-mineral-chime.32292.wav` is rendered through
  `npm run build-audio` (never hand-written) and its SHA-256 is committed in
  `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`.
- `npm run build-audio:verify` passes, including every pre-existing asset and
  `scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` (the new cue is a player cue, so it adds no
  `AMPLITUDE_TIERS` key).
- A unit test measures the baked WAV's peak sample (16-bit PCM peak / 32768,
  following the reader pattern in `scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts`) and
  asserts it is **≤ 0.2**, the documented player-cue ceiling (GDD §7.3).
- `playMineralCollectChimeSound(step)` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts`
  and dispatches through the single `playCue` funnel with
  `{ rate: mineralChimeRate(step) }`, so it inherits the shared per-cue voice
  limiter, the master gain and `setSfxVolume`/`setSfxMuted`; with no
  `AudioContext` it is a silent no-op that never throws. No parallel rate
  limiter and no second volume constant are added.
- The existing contract tests (`src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`,
  `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`) pass with the new cue, proving the
  export, the manifest entry and the resolvable asset are all wired.
- The chime is subtle and quiet: the baked asset peaks at ≤ 0.2 (the documented player-cue ceiling in GDD §7.3) with a stated target level in the recipe header, and it obeys the global SFX volume/mute settings and the shared per-cue voice limiter, degrading to a silent no-op with no `AudioContext`.
- The new cue is delivered through the existing ToneForge baked pipeline: a new `aihell-mineral-chime` recipe (next free seed 32292), a manifest entry, a deterministic baked WAV plus committed checksum, and `npm run build-audio:verify` passes unchanged for every pre-existing asset.
- Tests cover the cue (export + manifest + resolvable baked asset); the escalation state machine and the shared wiring in the game and in the gyms are covered by their own items.

## Minimal implementation

1. Author the recipe (triangle/sine partial + gentle decay + quiet shimmer),
   set gains so the render peaks ≤ 0.2.
2. Add the manifest entry, run the bake, commit WAV + checksum.
3. Add `playMineralCollectChimeSound` next to `playMineralTinkleSound` in
   `src/audio/effects.ts` and the peak assertion test.

**Key Files:**

- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-mineral-chime.yaml` — new recipe.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue entry.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-mineral-chime.32292.wav`, `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — baked asset + checksum.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playMineralCollectChimeSound(step)`.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`, `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts` — cue/asset contract coverage (plus the new peak test).

## Dependencies

Depends on **Pure mineral chime escalation state machine** (the rate helper the
wrapper uses). Blocks the wiring item.

## Risks

Baking needs the local ToneForge CLI (`../ToneForge`, present on this machine).
If it is unavailable the implementer must stop and report the blocker — never
hand-write a WAV.

# One shared chime dispatch on every player pickup

Part of **Chime whenever a mineral is collected** (AH-0MWNHEIV90047V91). Wires
the cue into gameplay **once**: one shared dispatch point in the combat core,
consumed by the game and every gym, so no scene keeps a copy of the escalation
rule (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `CombatCoreScene` owns the single dispatch: one `protected` method (e.g.
  `noteMineralCollected()`) that reads the scene clock (`this.time.now`, game
  time — pauses with the scene, never wall time), advances the shared state
  machine and plays `playMineralCollectChimeSound(step)` exactly once.
- Every **player** collection path calls that one method exactly once per
  collected mineral — `PlayScene._collectMineral`,
  `GymFormationScene._collectMineral` (and every formation-gym subclass
  through it), `GymLevel._collectMineral`,
  `GymPowerUpsUtility._collectGymMineral`, and the bespoke leveling loops
  `GymWeaponLeveling._collectMineralsOverlapping` /
  `GymPowerUpLeveling._collectMineralsOverlapping`.
- **Enemy absorption is silent**: a mineral absorbed by an enemy entity plays
  no chime, asserted in the game and in a gym (the feedback is player-only).
- The streak is reset in the shared `resetRunState()` **and**
  `teardownRunState()` seams, so a restarted run and a scene shutdown both
  start from the base pitch (the scene instance is reused across restarts).
- A repo-wide guard test (using `collectProductionSourceFiles` from
  `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts`) proves the ladder/gap/cue reference exists
  in exactly **one** production site — no scene re-implements the escalation
  or calls `playMineralCollectChimeSound` directly.
- A dense-burst test collects many minerals in one frame (a scattered pair, a
  Mineral Scoop sweep and a 100-mineral gym field) and asserts the shared voice
  limiter bounds the admitted voices (`MAX_CONCURRENT_CUE_VOICES`) with no
  throw and no second throttle.
- A gym↔game parity test boots the real `PlayScene` and a real gym, collects a
  mineral in each, and observes the same cue dispatch (no scene-local
  divergence); `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` is updated only if a divergence is
  introduced (expected: none — every scene inherits the shared core).
- The collection/economy behaviour is unchanged: no mineral value, drop rule,
  collection geometry, scoring or telemetry change (existing tests stay green).
- Every player mineral pickup plays a quiet chime — one chime per collected mineral, on every path that credits the mineral hold, through one shared implementation — so a `PlayScene` run and any gym behave identically.
- Enemy absorption plays no chime — the feedback is player-only, so an enemy hoovering up a mineral never reads as a player reward.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the shared dispatch method + the two resets to
   `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`.
2. Add the single call in each of the six collection paths (one line each —
   no logic).
3. Add the wiring, absorption-silence, reset and dense-burst tests; add the
   defined-once guard case to the parity guard test file.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared dispatch + run-reset/teardown resets.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — one call per player collection path.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralChime.parity.test.ts` (new) — shared-dispatch, absorption-silence, reset and defined-once guards.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — existing wiring/equivalence guards.

## Architecture decision (recorded, no producer input needed)

The brief offered two candidate single dispatch points: the shared collection
layer (`src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`) or a shared core hook
(`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`). **This item uses the shared core hook.**

Why: `collectMinerals` is deliberately Phaser-free (`@module
scenes/core/mineralLayer`) and is consumed by the headless eval arena tests
(`src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts`); firing audio from it would inject a
side effect into the pure collection layer and leave the two bespoke leveling
gyms' own overlap loops uncovered anyway. Every player-collection path in the
game and in the gyms extends `CombatCoreScene` (`PlayScene`, `GymLevel`,
`GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymPowerUpLeveling` via `CombatScene`;
`GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` directly), so a hook there covers
all six paths with one line each, gets the scene clock (`this.time.now`, game
time) for free, and reuses the existing `resetRunState()` /
`teardownRunState()` seams for the streak reset — no new lifecycle hook.

This is a deliberate, documented narrowing of the brief's "preferably from the
shared collection layer": the escalation *logic* still lives exactly once (in
`src/audio/mineralChime.ts` + the one core hook), which is the parity rule that
matters; only the six call sites are per-scene, and the defined-once guard test
above enforces that they carry no logic.

## Dependencies

Depends on **Pure mineral chime escalation state machine** and **Baked
aihell-mineral-chime cue**. Blocks the documentation item.

# Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading

## Problem statement

The target-aware config (hangar) screen marks **every** weapon row with its
matchup against the chosen hex's boss — green `▲ EFFECTIVE` when the boss is
weak to it, red `▼ RESISTED` when the boss resists it — but it does so even for
rows the player **cannot act on**: weapons they cannot buy (short of salvage,
`NEED 40 min`, or still ring-gated, `RING 2`) and owned weapons whose pricey
upgrade they cannot afford. Highlighting a recommendation the player cannot act
on reads as "buy this", so the intel lies about what is available right now.

## Users

- **The new player with no salvage** — "I have 0 minerals; every weapon row is
  lit up as if I could bring or upgrade it. Only light up what I can act on."
- **The ring-1 player** — "A ring-2 weapon is shown in bright red as if my
  loadout choice matters; I cannot buy it yet."
- **The accessibility-minded player** — "The matchup must still be readable
  without colour wherever it is shown." (Repo CVD policy: never colour-only.)
- **The producer/maintainer** — "One shared model decides the highlight, so the
  game and `GymHangar` cannot drift and no scene owns a second rule."

Example user stories:

- As a player with no salvage, I still read the boss's intel and the `▲`/`▼`
  verdicts, but only the rows I could actually buy or upgrade are highlighted.
- As a player with enough salvage for one weapon, that row is highlighted and
  the ones I cannot afford render as ordinary disabled rows.
- As a player equipping a weapon I already own, the `LOADOUT` column keeps its
  full matchup highlight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Rows with no available action are not highlighted.** In the hangar screen's
  unlock tree, a `weapon` row the player cannot act on right now — purchase
  states `unaffordable` (`NEED … min`) and `gated` (`RING n`), and upgrade
  states `upgrade-unaffordable` and `capped` (`MAX`) — renders with **no**
  strong/weak colour and **no** strong/weak background tint, keeping the
  ordinary row styling (muted colour, its price/shortfall or `MAX` intact).
- **Rows with an available action keep their highlight.** A `weapon` row whose
  own action is available — a `buyable` purchase row and an `upgradable` upgrade
  row — keeps exactly today's behaviour: `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` marker,
  strong/weak colour and tint.
- **The `LOADOUT` column is unchanged.** Every starting-weapon row in the
  deployment selector (owned weapons, always toggleable) keeps its marker,
  colour and tint, because equipping/unequipping it is always available.
- **The marker stays on every weapon row.** The `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED`
  text tag is appended wherever the weapon has a strong/weak verdict, including
  the non-highlighted rows, so the intel stays readable without colour (CVD
  policy) and only the colour/tint follows affordability.
- **The shared model decides, and the gym agrees.** Whether a row is highlighted
  is published by `buildHangarScreenModel`/`buildHangarUnlockRows` (data beside
  the existing `matchup` verdict), never derived from the render-time
  interactive/actionable flag, so the read-only `GymHangar` render shows exactly
  the game's highlight; a test asserts the model, the game render and the gym
  render agree for the same payload.
- **Automated tests cover the matrix.** Model-level and render-level tests for
  `buyable` + strong/weak, `unaffordable` + strong/weak, `gated` + strong/weak,
  `upgradable` + strong/weak, `upgrade-unaffordable` + strong/weak, `capped` +
  strong/weak, and a `LOADOUT` row of each strength; plus a test that a
  non-highlighted row keeps its marker, price and shortfall.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, GDD §8.2, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A player choosing a loadout only sees the boss-counter highlight on weapon rows
they can actually act on right now, while the `▲`/`▼` intel stays readable
everywhere — so the green/red marks are a promise the player can keep.

## Assumptions (documented; producer may override at review)

- **A1 — "Cannot buy" = `unaffordable` or `gated`.** Both mean the purchase
  cannot happen now (`canBuy` returns `unaffordable` for a salvage shortfall and
  `gated` for a not-yet-reached ring), so neither row is highlighted.
  (Producer Q2 = (a).)
- **A2 — Marker retained, colour suppressed.** A non-highlighted row keeps the
  `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` text marker and only loses the colour and backing
  tint, so it reads as a normal row whose matchup is still legible without
  colour. (Producer Q1 = (a).)
- **A3 — LOADOUT yes, upgrade tree no.** The `LOADOUT` equipped/unequipped column
  keeps its highlight for owned weapons (the action is always available); in the
  main upgrade/purchase tree the highlight follows the row's **own** action, so
  an owned weapon whose upgrade is `upgrade-unaffordable` (or `capped`) is **not**
  highlighted, while an `upgradable` one is. (Producer Q3: "equipped/unequipped
  column yes, main selection for upgrade no".)
- **A3.1 — `capped` (`MAX`) counts as "no available action".** A maxed row has
  nothing left to buy, so it is not highlighted; the player still sees the
  weapon highlighted in the `LOADOUT` column. Recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in
  case the producer would rather a maxed weapon keep its highlight.
- **A4 — Display only.** Prices, ring gating, ownership, the matchup resolver
  (`src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`) and the `TARGET INTEL` block are
  unchanged; this item changes only which rows are highlighted (parent
  AH-0MWMRWCY2001HWGR assumption A7 stands — the mechanical matchup is
  AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ).
- **A5 — No new persistence.** No payload schema or store change.
- **A6 — Existing fixtures must be re-baselined.** Today's matchup tests use a
  0-salvage payload whose weapons are all **owned**, so those rows are
  `upgrade-unaffordable` and (per A3) lose their colour: the rendered-colour
  assertion for `buy:spread` in `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` must change, and
  a fixture with salvage must be added to keep a positive highlight assertion.
  The `matchup` verdict and the `▲`/`▼` labels survive unchanged.

## Constraints

- **Model, not render, decides the highlight.** `renderHangarScreen` reports
  every row non-actionable in a read-only render (the gym), so keying the
  highlight off `actionable` would silently blank every mark in `GymHangar` and
  break gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **One shared code path.** No second matchup/highlight rule in `HangarScene`,
  `GymHangar` or the map; the pure model plus the one renderer stay the only
  place the rule lives.
- **Never colour-only.** The glyph tag stays on every weapon row with a verdict;
  a suppressed row must remain an ordinary readable row (price + shortfall, or
  `MAX`), not an unexplained blank.
- **No layout change.** No new rows or sections; `hangarLowestRowY` /
  bottom-row geometry are untouched.
- **No economy change.** The affordability verdicts are the economy's own
  (`canBuy`, `costToUpgrade`); this item only reads them.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Auto-buying the counter weapon, hiding non-weapon rows,
  dimming the `TARGET INTEL` block, or changing prices/gating are out of scope —
  record them as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Risks

- **Gym-parity regression (high).** Deriving the highlight from render-time
  `actionable` would blank every mark in the read-only gym; mitigated by
  publishing the decision in the model and asserting it in `GymHangar.test.ts`.
- **Test re-baseline churn (medium, expected).** Two existing tests assert a
  colour on rows that are now non-highlighted (0-salvage owned weapons); they
  must be updated deliberately, with a salvage-bearing fixture keeping the
  positive case covered.
- **Player surprise on `MAX` rows (low).** A maxed weapon loses its tree
  highlight (A3.1); the `LOADOUT` column still shows it, so the intel is never
  lost — flagged as an OPEN QUESTION for override.
- **Fixture blindness (medium).** No current fixture has a weapon it cannot
  afford, which is why this slipped through the parent epic; the new matrix adds
  one deliberately.

## Existing state

- `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) resolves a
  `matchup` for **every** `weapon`-kind row, regardless of the economy verdict,
  via `resolveBossMatchup(entry.weaponId, target)`, and appends the marker with
  `withMatchupMarker(...)`.
- The renderer's `rowColour(actionable, matchup)` returns
  `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` / `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR` **before** consulting
  `actionable`, and `rowBackground(matchup)` tints the row — so an
  `unaffordable` (`NEED 40 min`), `gated` (`RING 2`), `upgrade-unaffordable` or
  `capped` (`MAX`) weapon row renders in the bright highlight colour with its
  tint even though nothing can be bought on it.
- `HangarUnlockRow.state` already carries the economy verdict (`owned`, `gated`,
  `unaffordable`, `buyable`, `upgradable`, `upgrade-unaffordable`, `capped`);
  the information needed is present, it is simply not consulted by the highlight.
- `HangarWeaponOption` rows are built from `unlockedWeapons` only (owned, always
  actionable), so the `LOADOUT` column is already always highlighted — and per
  A3 keeps that.
- `GymHangar` renders the same model with **no handlers**, so every rendered row
  reports `actionable: false` while showing the game's colours; the highlight
  must therefore be model data (`src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` pins parity).
- Tests today: `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` ("marks every weapon row …",
  "renders the intel section, the glyph tags and the matchup colours") and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` ("renders the known target intel and ▲/▼
  matchup marks read-only") assert the marker/colour on rows from a 0-salvage
  fixture whose weapons are all **owned** (upgrade rows).

## Desired change

- **Publish the highlight decision in the model.** Beside `matchup`, expose
  whether that verdict should be *highlighted* for this row — true when the row's
  own action is available (`buyable` purchase, `upgradable` upgrade, and every
  `LOADOUT` weapon option), false for `unaffordable`, `gated`,
  `upgrade-unaffordable` and `capped` unlock rows — derived from the economy
  verdicts already on the row (no new economy rule).
- **Render from that flag.** `rowColour` / `rowBackground` consult the highlight
  flag (never the render-time `actionable` flag), so a non-highlighted row falls
  back to the existing row styling while highlighted rows keep today's colour
  and tint. The `▲`/`▼` marker keeps being appended unconditionally by
  `withMatchupMarker`.
- **Cover the matrix with tests** in `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` (model +
  render, with a salvage-bearing fixture for the positive cases) and the gym
  parity case in `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`.
- **Update the docs** that promise the current unconditional marking
  (`README.md` hangar/hex-map paragraphs, GDD §8.2, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`,
  `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *Known-ahead intel*).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — the per-row highlight flag in
  `buildHangarUnlockRows` / `buildHangarWeaponOptions`, and the colour/tint
  decision in `rowColour` / `rowBackground`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` — model + render tests for the `buyable` /
  `unaffordable` / `gated` / `upgradable` / `upgrade-unaffordable` / `capped` /
  `LOADOUT` matrix, and the re-baselined colour assertion.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — parity: the gym renders the same
  suppressed highlight for a non-actionable row.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — record the highlight rule for `GymHangar`.
- `README.md` — the hangar and hex-map paragraphs that describe the marks.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2 config-screen intel paragraph.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — § *Known-ahead intel* (the config screen
  marks "each weapon row").

## Related work

- **AH-0MWMRWCY2001HWGR — When starting a Hex War battle show the ship config
  screen** (completed): the parent epic that introduced the target-aware config
  screen and the unconditional marks this item narrows (children
  AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y pure resolver, AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN model/render,
  AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 gym parity + docs).
- **AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y — Weapon-vs-boss matchup resolver** (completed): the
  pure `resolveBossMatchup` verdict this item presents differently — unchanged.
- **AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat**
  (open): owns the mechanical matchup; this item stays display-only.
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY — Post-MVP Hangar War: hull upgrade bays as a reward
  axis** (open): future economy surface; unaffected but must not inherit a
  misleading highlight.
- Automated find-related report also surfaced `README.md`, `docs/Game Design
  Document.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` as keyword matches
  (documentation touch points).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Asked in-session of the producer; the item was flagged `needsProducerReview`
while the questions were open and is released on their answers.

- **Q1 — Should a non-highlighted weapon row also lose the ▲/▼ text marker, or
  only the colour/tint?**
  Options: (a) keep the marker, suppress colour + tint; (b) hide marker and
  colour together; (c) keep the marker in the muted colour with a `· LOCKED`
  suffix.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the item asks for colour to follow affordability, and
  keeping the tag preserves the CVD-safe intel the parent epic required.
  **Answer (producer): (a)** — keep the marker, suppress only the colour and the
  backing tint. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session. Now recorded as
  AC4 and assumption A2.
- **Q2 — Does "not able to buy" include ring-gated rows (`RING 2`), or only rows
  short of salvage (`NEED … min`)?**
  Options: (a) both; (b) only `unaffordable`.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a gated row is equally unbuyable now, and `canBuy`
  already reports it as `gated` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:528`).
  **Answer (producer): (a)** — both, any row the player cannot buy now. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session. Now recorded as AC1 and assumption A1.
- **Q3 — Do owned weapons keep their highlight when their *upgrade* is
  unaffordable or capped?**
  Options: (a) yes — ownership makes the weapon usable now; (b) no — mute the
  row.
  **Recommended:** (a) (ownership makes the weapon usable now).
  **Answer (producer): split — "if you mean in the equipped/unequipped column
  yes, if you mean in the main selection for upgrade, no."** So the `LOADOUT`
  equipped/unequipped column keeps the highlight for owned weapons, while the
  main purchase/upgrade tree highlights only rows whose own action is available
  (`buyable` / `upgradable`). Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session.
  This **supersedes** the earlier recommended (a) and is recorded as AC3/AC2 and
  assumption A3. Research: the 0-salvage fixtures make those tree rows
  `upgrade-unaffordable`, so their rendered-colour assertions must be
  re-baselined (assumption A6).
- **Q3.1 — Does a `capped` (`MAX`) row count as "no available action"?**
  **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION (producer) — drafted as "yes, not highlighted"
  (A3.1), because the row has nothing left to buy while the `LOADOUT` column
  still shows the weapon's matchup highlighted. Overriding this only changes one
  state in the highlight predicate.

# Replace in-repo video processing with the `vidc` CLI

**Issue type:** task · **Priority:** high

## User story

As a maintainer, I want AI_Hell to stop owning its own FFmpeg video-processing
pipeline and instead delegate video compilation to the `vidc` CLI
(`video_compiler`), so that video processing has a single maintained home and
this repository contains only game, capture and telemetry code.

## Background

The repository's post-capture video processing lives in the promo compiler:
`scripts/compile-promo.mjs` (FFmpeg argv planning, per-junction
`xfade`/`acrossfade`, VP9/Opus encoding, probe + brightness + pace validation)
plus its pool inventory (`scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs`) and their tests and
docs. `vidc` (cloned at `../video_compiler`) is the replacement engine: it
discovers clips, orders them, probes with `ffprobe`, and renders one normalised
MP4 with a single FFmpeg invocation, supporting formats and render profiles.

Capture (Playwright `MediaRecorder` → WebM), the capture-time probe/seek/remux
helpers and the action-intensity series export are **capture tooling**, not the
post-capture video-processing pipeline, and stay.

## Decisions

- No backward compatibility: the bespoke compiler, its selection/validation
  logic, its manifests and its tests are deleted rather than kept beside vidc.
- Deliverables become MP4 (vidc's native output), replacing the legacy
  VP9/Opus WebM deliverables.
- Missing vidc capabilities surface during this migration are tracked in the
  `video_compiler` project as **high priority** items and synced:
  - `VC-0MWNOFIBI007J8UK` — render integration honours clip bounds
    (`source_range` in/out trimming).
  - `VC-0MWNW4SPX002J2SE` — transition-aware filter graph (per-junction
    `xfade`/`acrossfade`).
  - `VC-0MWNW4SYJ009XMIP` — compile/render transition hand-off.
  (The automated highlight selection is intentionally dropped with the legacy
  pipeline; vidc owns editing.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` and its type/test files are removed, along
      with `scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs` and its type/test files.
- [ ] A new thin renderer (`scripts/render-promo.mjs`) forwards to
      `vidc render` (binary overridable via `--vidc` / `VIDC_BIN`), forwards
      subprocess output and exit code, supports `--dir`, `--output`,
      `--pattern`, `--format` (repeatable), `--fade-duration`, `--resolution`,
      `--fps`, `--overwrite`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--help`.
- [ ] The renderer is covered by unit tests (mocked subprocess) for argv
      forwarding, exit-code propagation, missing-binary remediation and
      `--json`/`--dry-run` passthrough.
- [ ] `package.json` drops the legacy `list:pool` entry and points
      `capture:promo` at the new renderer.
- [ ] The legacy video-processing documentation is removed: the
      "Pool inventory" and "Compiling a promo package" sections of
      `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, and the highlight-selection / pace-band
      sections (§7.5, §7.6) of `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`, with
      cross-references and `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts` updated or removed.
- [ ] Doc guards that imported constants from the deleted compiler
      (`src/actionIntensityDocs.test.ts`, `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts`,
      `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts`) are updated to use the surviving
      editorial-category vocabulary.
- [ ] `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate pass.

## Impact

Maintainers no longer carry a bespoke FFmpeg promo pipeline in AI_Hell: video
compilation is delegated to the maintained `vidc` CLI.

## Assumptions

- Capture recording, capture-time probing/remuxing and action-intensity series
  export are capture tooling, not the post-capture video-processing pipeline.
- MP4 is acceptable as the deliverable container for promos.
- Automated highlight selection is out of scope after the migration and is
  removed with the legacy compiler; vidc's timeline editing is the forward path
  once its trimming/transition items land.

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`, `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts`
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`, `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts`
- `scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs`, `scripts/list-capture-pool.d.mts`, `scripts/list-capture-pool.test.ts`
- `scripts/render-promo.mjs`, `scripts/render-promo.d.mts`, `scripts/render-promo.test.ts`
- `package.json`
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`, `README.md`
- `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts`, `src/actionIntensityDocs.test.ts`
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs`, `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts`
