# Bot needs to be more accurate with its navigation — Intake Brief

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** bug · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

The competent bot's aim **lead** is effectively not running for the enemies it shoots at. `engage`
aims at `interceptPoint(...)` only when its chosen target exposes `vx`/`vy`, but the snapshot only
carries velocity for entities with a physics body — in practice `Asteroid` and `LaneTraffic`
(`src/entities/Asteroid.ts:418`, `src/entities/LaneTraffic.ts:145`). Every formation, `chaser`,
`diver` and `patroller` enemy moves by scripted position updates with no `vx`/`vy`
(`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:121`), so the bot aims at the target's **current** position and the shot
arrives after the target has moved — the ship "often misses its target". Where a lead *is* solved,
the trajectory model is a constant-velocity straight line and the projectile speed used for the
time of flight is the **enemy** bullet speed (`assumedBulletSpeed` = 200 px/s), not the ship's own
350 px/s, so the lead is over-estimated by 75 %. Meanwhile the bot already owns a better motion
model for the same entities — the per-hazard velocity/curvature tracker plus the movement-class
trajectory sampler that hazard avoidance runs — so the fix is to apply the **same calculations to
aim as are used to predict movement**, and to give the aim a small, configurable error so it is
deliberately imperfect rather than accidentally wrong.

## Users

- **Player watching the attract/demo bot** (primary): expects a pilot whose shots connect with the
  enemy it is chasing, not one that keeps missing a curving target.
- **Producer tuning the bot in `GymBotTuning`** (secondary): wants the lead/aim error as live knobs
  and a reproducible, test-backed accuracy number rather than a subjective "looks better".
- **Developer** (secondary): wants one trajectory definition shared by prediction and aim so the
  two cannot drift apart.

### Example user stories

- As a **viewer of the demo**, I want the bot's shots to hit the chaser that is curving toward the
  ship, so the demo reads as competent rather than broken.
- As a **producer**, I want a configurable aim error so the bot is beatable and human-looking, and a
  live slider to trade accuracy for fallibility.
- As a **developer**, I want the aim solve to consume the same velocity and movement-class
  prediction as hazard avoidance, so I fix prediction once and both features benefit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Aim lead uses the bot's own motion estimate, not the snapshot's.** The `engage` aim solve
  resolves its target's velocity from the bot-side tracker
  (`trackHazardVelocities` → `BotWorld.hazards[].vx/vy/curvature`, the same estimate the hazard
  predictor consumes) instead of the raw `BotEnemy.vx/vy` field. A moving formation/`chaser`/
  `diver`/`patroller` target that exposes no snapshot velocity is therefore led. When no estimate
  exists yet (cold start, stale, or an id-less fixture target) the solve reduces **exactly** to
  today's behaviour (aim at the current position).
- **AC2 — Solve inputs come from live physics.** The intercept solve takes the **player's**
  projectile speed and the **ship's live turn time**, not the bot's assumptions:
  `assumedBulletSpeed` (200 px/s, an enemy-bullet tell constant) is replaced as the aim
  time-of-flight input by the ship's live projectile speed (350 px/s `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` /
  per-weapon speed, carried through the snapshot seam the way `getThrusterConfig()`/
  `getRotationConfig()` already are), and the fixed `aimLeadAlignSeconds` alignment term is
  derived from the live rotation model (`angularStopDisplacement` + rotation accel/decel) with the
  constant retained only as the no-config fallback. A unit test pins 200 → 350 and the
  turn-time derivation.
- **AC3 — Predict the trajectory the target will actually fly.** For a target with a fitted velocity
  and a known movement class, the intercept point is solved by advancing the target along the
  **sampled class trajectory** (`advanceHazardMotion`, the single definition of each class's
  motion, already used by `predictMinimumSeparation`) and re-estimating time of flight each
  iteration; `roamer`/unknown class/disabled motion model reproduces the constant-velocity solve
  bit-for-bit, and a stationary target reproduces the current-position aim bit-for-bit. Wrap-aware
  (torus) behaviour from AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15 is preserved.
- **AC4 — Configurable, self-correcting aim error.** A new live-tuned `aimErrorRad` (radians,
  default small — ≈0.02 rad — and applied only to intents flagged as **aim**, never to
  survival/evade/travel) perturbs the committed aim bearing from the governor's dedicated seeded
  aim-error RNG stream (deterministic per run seed, no draw at `0`, so `0` is byte-for-byte today's
  behaviour). It is independent of the existing `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` degradation. The error is
  **adaptive, not fixed** (producer answer Q1): every confirmed hit on the engaged target multiplies
  the current error by `aimErrorDecay` (default ≈0.5, floored at 0), so a bot that keeps hitting
  zeroes in; the error is restored to `aimErrorRad` only after a **repositioning move** — the ship
  having moved `aimErrorResetDistance` px (default ≈60, torus-aware, measured from its position at
  the last hit) or having changed engagement target. All three knobs are live sliders via
  `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` / `GymBotTuning` and persisted in `src/data/bot-tuning.json`; the hit
  signal arrives through one shared scene seam (AC6), so the game and every gym feed it identically.
- **AC5 — Accuracy is measured, not asserted.** A deterministic headless aim-accuracy harness
  (seeded, fixed 60 Hz, a fixed seed list of at least three seeds, one scenario per movement class)
  reports shots fired / shots hit / mean miss distance for the new solve against the pre-change
  baseline, and a regression test asserts the pooled hit rate is strictly higher than the baseline
  and the mean miss distance lower, with `aimErrorRad = 0`. The measured before/after numbers are
  recorded on the work item.
- **AC6 — Single-sourced and gym-parity clean.** All behaviour lives in the shared `src/ai` code
  (plus the snapshot seam and the hit seam); `PlayScene`, `GymBotTuning` and every bot-bearing gym
  consume the same code, with no per-scene copy and no gym/game divergence introduced. The aim-hit
  signal is published from the shared `CombatScene` collision path — a hook beside the existing
  `onEnemyDestroyed` / `finaliseEnemyKill` seam (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:662`), plus the
  overridable `CombatScene.onEnemyDestroyed` precedent at line 1195 — never re-implemented per
  scene.
- **AC7 — Docs and tests.** `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.8 (rotation skills / lead) and the §12 knob
  list describe the new solve, the new knob and the accuracy harness; unit tests cover the solve,
  the speed/turn inputs and the error draw, and `src/ai/botRotationSkills.integration.test.ts` (or a
  sibling integration test) exercises the end-to-end aim. All related documentation is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
  Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The demo bot's shots now land on the enemy it is actually chasing — including curving and
formation enemies it currently aims behind — the bot visibly zeroes in while a burst keeps hitting
and gets its wobble back when it repositions, and designers get sliders to dial in how fallible it
looks.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** Shared behaviour stays in `src/ai/`; `PlayScene`, the shared
  `src/scenes/core/` code and every gym scene consume the same functions.
- **No physics constants in the bot layer.** Live ship values arrive through the `BotSnapshot` seam
  (the `getRotationConfig()` / `getThrusterConfig()` precedent), never hard-coded in `src/ai/`.
- **Deterministic and cheap.** No wall clock, seeded RNG only, same inputs → same output; the per-tick
  path stays allocation-free/bounded (it runs for every engage tick inside the 50-enemy perf
  envelope).
- **Telemetry schema unchanged.** Accuracy is measured in the test/harness layer; no new telemetry
  event kinds are introduced by this item.
- **Out of scope (record, do not absorb).** Re-driving the real enemy entities from
  `advanceHazardMotion` (a substantially larger predictor/entity unification); telemetry
  shots-fired/hit events; per-pod orbit-weapon lead; enemy aim accuracy (this item is the ship's
  aim).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — stale or cold tracked estimate.** The tracker needs two ticks of history, so the first
  engagement tick has no velocity. Mitigation: the documented exact fallback to the current-position
  aim, covered by a unit test.
- **Risk — the class model is not the entity's real movement.** `advanceHazardMotion` is the
  predictor's own definition; a class whose real entity diverges would still mis-lead. Mitigation:
  the AC5 harness measures per class so a diver/chaser regression is visible, and unifying the
  entities with the model is recorded as an explicit follow-up rather than silently absorbed.
- **Risk — over-leading a reverser.** Formation enemies drift and reverse; a long lead on an enemy
  that turns back over-leads further than no lead. Mitigation: the class sampler's bounded horizon
  and iteration count, plus the `aimLeadEnabled` off-switch, and the per-class measurement in AC5.
- **Risk — per-tick cost.** The aim solve runs on every engage tick near the 50-enemy perf envelope.
  Mitigation: reuse the existing bounded sampler (`HAZARD_MOTION_MAX_SAMPLES`) and its scratch
  buffers; no per-tick allocation.
- **Risk — a hit signal that lies.** Counting hits on *any* enemy (a stray bullet, an AOE, a ram)
  would sharpen the aim for the wrong reason. Mitigation: only a hit on the **engaged target** decays
  the error, and the repositioning reset keeps a streak from surviving a change of victim.
- **Risk — repositioning definition mismatch.** A distance-only rule could re-arm the error mid-fight
  during a slow strafe, or never re-arm it in a hugging fight. Mitigation: `aimErrorResetDistance` is
  a live knob, the target change also re-arms, and the AC5 harness reports the shot mix (led vs
  unled) so the rule is tuned on numbers.
- **Risk — scope creep into entity/predictor unification**, telemetry shot events or weapon-specific
  lead. Mitigation: all three are listed as out of scope; they become linked work items if wanted.
- **Assumption** — the turn actuator (deadband, inertia-aware hold) is correct; only the aim target
  changes. **Assumption** — 350 px/s is the representative ship projectile speed (pod weapons at
  300 px/s are accepted as within the aim error). **Resolved by the producer (Q1)** — the error is a
  dedicated `aimErrorRad` that decays on hits and re-arms on a repositioning move.

## Existing state

- Aim lead today: `engage` calls `interceptPoint` only when `best.point.vx/vy` are non-zero
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts:212`), passing `t.assumedBulletSpeed` (200 px/s) as the
  **projectile** speed and `t.aimLeadAlignSeconds` (0.25 s default, 0.35 s shipped tuning) as the
  alignment term.
- `interceptPoint` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts:197`) is a pure constant-velocity
  iterated lead; wrap-aware since AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15, but it never consults a movement class.
- Shot speed: travelling player bullets use `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 350`
  (`src/core/constants.ts:378`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:1114`); pod bullets use 300
  (`src/utils/weapons.ts:689`). `assumedBulletSpeed = 200`
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts:444`) is described in
  `src/ai/tuningFields.ts:126` as the *enemy*-bullet speed for fire tells — it is reused here for
  the ship's time of flight.
- Motion model that already exists and is already trusted for prediction:
  `trackHazardVelocities` (`src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts:178`, velocity + curvature from a
  bounded position history), `resolveEnemyMovementClass`
  (`src/ai/framework/enemyMovementClass.ts:75`, archetype → class mirror of
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) and `advanceHazardMotion`
  (`src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts:595`), consumed by `predictMinimumSeparation`. Its
  docstring states the evaluation arena advances live hostiles with the same call, so prediction and
  "actual movement" are meant to be one definition.
- Aim error that already exists: `BotInputGovernor` perturbs aim-flagged intents by
  `maxAimErrorRad × (1 − skill)` from a dedicated seeded stream
  (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts:943`), default `skill = 1` (off).
- The ship auto-fires (no aim gate on the trigger), so accuracy is entirely "is the nose where the
  target will be".
- Hit feedback does not exist: player-bullet damage is applied in
  `CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:576`) and kills are
  finalised once in `finaliseEnemyKill` / `onEnemyDestroyed` (`:662`, `:1195`), but nothing tells the
  bot whether an aimed shot connected — `BotSnapshot.player` (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:76`) carries no
  hit signal, so AC4's adaptive error needs a new seam.
- Shot accuracy is not currently measured: the evaluation harness has kills and player hits but no
  shots-fired event (`docs/TELEMETRY.md` §event kinds).

## Desired change

- Resolve the engaged target's motion from the tracker (AC1) and keep the raw-snapshot path as the
  cold-start fallback.
- Carry the ship's live projectile speed and rotation config through the snapshot seam and feed the
  real values into the solve (AC2), plus the aim-hit count the governor needs for AC4.
- Add a class-aware intercept that samples `advanceHazardMotion`, converging time of flight against
  the sampled trajectory, and reduce exactly to the legacy solve when the class/estimate is
  unknown (AC3).
- Add `aimErrorRad` as a seeded, aim-only, live-tunable error that decays on confirmed hits and
  re-arms on a repositioning move (AC4), fed by a new shared aim-hit seam (AC6).
- Add the headless accuracy harness and record its before/after numbers (AC5).
- Update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and the knob documentation (AC7).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — `engage` aim solve: consume the tracked motion and
  class, pass the live shot speed and turn time.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `interceptPoint`: add the class-sampled variant and
  the live turn-time input, preserving exact fallbacks.
- `src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts` — reuse `advanceHazardMotion` (no new trajectory code).
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — expose the engaged target's tracker estimate to the aim path
  (hazards already carry `vx`/`vy`/`curvature`/`movementClass`).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — carry the ship's live projectile speed, rotation config (if not already
  present) and the aim-hit count through the structural source seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — publish the aim-hit hook beside `onEnemyDestroyed` /
  `finaliseEnemyKill` (single-sourced for the game and every gym).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — thread the hit count (and the
  reposition state the governor derives from the snapshot) into the bot without local logic.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`, `src/data/bot-tuning.json` —
  the new knob plus the `assumedBulletSpeed` description fix.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — `aimErrorRad` / `aimErrorDecay` / `aimErrorResetDistance` in the
  governor tunables, the seeded draw and the hit-decay / reposition-reset state.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`, `behaviours.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botRotationSkills.integration.test.ts`, plus the new aim-accuracy harness — tests.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — §9.8 and the §12 knob table.

## Related work

- **Bot rotation skills (AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98)** — introduced the lead solve, the inertia-aware turn
  hold and the `skill` aim error; this item continues that work by fixing the solve's inputs.
- **Predict enemy movement (bot) (AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN)** — built the hazard velocity tracker this
  item reuses for aim.
- **Movement-class seam for bot hazards (AH-0MWM0C6OW006G5SE)**, **Class-shaped hazard trajectory
  prediction (AH-0MWM0C9F9006HNXV)**, **Sampled prediction in steering and kiting
  (AH-0MWM0CB2Q003Y6AB)** — the class model and sampler the aim solve should share.
- **Seam-aware aim and intercept (AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15)** — the torus solve that must be preserved.
- **Bot needs to be better at avoiding enemies (AH-0MWLUIOH9001XBJ3)** — the sibling play-testing
  item on prediction fidelity for *avoidance*; same diagnosis, different consumer.
- Duplicate check performed — no completed item already satisfies these acceptance criteria.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Questions were queued for the producer at intake time and answered in an interactive producer
reply (2026-11-21). The brief above reflects the accepted answers; the recommended option and the
producer's extra condition are recorded per entry.

- **Q1 (answered) — What should the configurable aim error be, and what should it default to?**
  - Options: (a) a new dedicated `aimErrorRad` (radians) applied to aim intents only, default small
    (≈0.02 rad), independent of the existing `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` degradation; (b) reuse
    `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` and simply ship a default `skill < 1`; (c) declare a per-shot *hit*
    probability and deliberately throw the shot wide on a failed roll.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — a dedicated knob leaves the existing skill degradation intact for
    "make the bot worse on purpose" and gives one unambiguous number to tune; (c) would be a
    different (probability) model and much harder to make believable.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **"(a) — but once the bot hits the error should be
    reduced until they make a repositioning move."** Source: producer reply in this session.
    Research: the governor already owns a dedicated seeded aim-error stream
    (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts:943`), so the decay/reset state lives beside it and needs no new RNG;
    shortening the error on a hit requires a hit signal the bot does not have today, so AC4 now
    carries the adaptive rule and AC6 the shared seam that feeds it. AC4 was rewritten to specify
    `aimErrorDecay` (multiplicative, floored at 0) and `aimErrorResetDistance` (the repositioning
    move), so both halves of the producer's condition are testable.
- **Q2 (answered) — What does "the same calculations for predicting movement as those used in
  actual movement" mean in scope?**
  - Options: (a) reuse the bot-side trajectory model the hazard predictor already uses (tracked
    velocity/curvature + `advanceHazardMotion`), leaving the enemy entities untouched; (b) also
    re-drive the real enemy entities from `advanceHazardMotion` so prediction and entity code are
    literally the same call site (much larger, touches every enemy and gym).
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it delivers the requested prediction fidelity in the bot layer only, with
    no entity/gym churn; (b) is the natural follow-up once (a) proves the model is faithful.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(a)**. Source: producer reply in this session. (b) stays
    recorded as explicit out-of-scope in *Constraints* and becomes a follow-up item if wanted.
- **Q3 (answered) — How should "more accurate" be evidenced?**
  - Options: (a) a deterministic headless harness reporting shots fired / hits / mean miss distance
    per movement class, with a regression assertion against the pre-change baseline; (b) unit-level
    assertions on the solve only (no end-to-end number); (c) add telemetry shot events and compare
    recorded runs.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it produces a number the producer can quote and needs no telemetry
    schema change; (c) is a much bigger change for the same evidence.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(a)**. Source: producer reply in this session. No
    telemetry schema change; the harness numbers are recorded on the work item as AC5's evidence.
- **Assumption (not a question): title scope.** The title says "navigation" while the seed body
  ("It often misses its target") is about aim. Researched `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts`,
  `steering.ts`, `botHumanLike.ts` and the snapshot seam (see *Existing state*); the defect found is
  target-prediction/aim accuracy, and the fix also tightens the ship's own turn-time prediction
  (which is navigation-adjacent). Treated as an aim/prediction-accuracy item.
- **Assumption: turn control is already adequate.** `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` (0.05 rad) and the
  inertia-aware turn hold from AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98 are assumed correct; this item changes what the
  nose is aimed at, not how the nose is turned.

## Plan: decomposition into features (2026-11-21)

Decomposed into **8 vertical slices** in test-first, dependency order. Each slice carries the code,
its tests and (where it changes behaviour) the documentation its own consumers read; a consolidated
documentation slice closes parent AC7 because the aim solve, the knob table and the harness are one

| 3 | Live physics inputs in the aim solve (AH-0MWR04ZDU0005O8J) | feature | AC2 | 2 | ~2h |
| 4 | Class-sampled intercept solve (AH-0MWR051U6003BDB9) | feature | AC3 | 3 | ~3h |
| 5 | Shared aim-hit seam (AH-0MWR054VE006YSLN) | feature | AC6 | 1 | ~2h |
| 6 | Adaptive aim error knobs (AH-0MWR057Q8004PBOD) | feature | AC4 (+AC6 delivery) | 4, 5 | ~3h |
| 7 | Accuracy regression proof and recorded numbers (AH-0MWR05EZE0044Z01) | task | AC5 (proof) | 1–4, 6 | ~2h |
| 8 | Aim solve documentation and knob docs (AH-0MWR05J320041SAA) | docs | AC7 | 1–6 | ~2h |

**Why this order**

- **Measurement first.** The harness (slice 1) and its pinned pre-change baseline exist before any
  behaviour changes, so "more accurate" is a comparison against a recorded number rather than an
  opinion, and slice 7 turns it into an assertion.
- **One aim call site at a time.** Slices 2 → 3 → 4 each touch `engage`'s aim solve; doing them
  serially means each lands with an exact-fallback parity test before the next changes the same
  lines.
- **The error is last.** The adaptive aim error (slice 6) consumes the hit signal from slice 5 and
  perturbs the solve from slice 4, so it cannot land before either.
- **Docs close the loop** after the behaviour is real (slice 8), and the docs assertions are what
  stop §9.8/§12 drifting from the code.

**Between slices:** review the next slice's description against what actually landed, update it
(and this table) before starting, and keep the per-class harness numbers on this item current.

**Estimate:** the plan-stage effort/risk run over the eight slices reports **Small / Medium**
(O 8.5 h · M 14.5 h · P 22 h → **14.33 h expected**, **18.33 h recommended**, 76 % confidence) — a
refinement of the intake estimate (10.25 h / 15.25 h) that now carries real per-slice inputs. The
item stays **Small** and **Medium** risk, so no plan-approval pause was required.

**Review outcome:** all seven parent acceptance criteria are owned by exactly one slice (AC5 by two:
measurement in slice 1, proof in slice 7), the AC coverage review returns `proceed`, and no new
clarifying questions were needed — the producer's intake answers (Q1–Q3, recorded in the Appendix
above) resolve every open choice.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-21 — created slices 1–8 with the table above; wired 15 dependency edges
  (2←1, 3←2, 4←3, 5←1, 6←4+5, 7←1–4+6, 8←1–6); appended the plan to the description; stage →
  `plan_complete` after the AC coverage review returned `proceed`.

### Appendix: planning-session questions

- **Q (plan, 2026-11-21) — are any further producer decisions needed to cut this into slices?**
  Answer: **no** — intake Q1 (dedicated `aimErrorRad` with decay-on-hit / re-arm-on-reposition,
  option a), Q2 (reuse the bot-side trajectory model, option a) and Q3 (deterministic headless
  accuracy harness, option a) are recorded in the Appendix above and settle every branch the
  decomposition faced. No follow-up questions were raised; nothing is left OPEN QUESTION at plan
  time. Source: this work item's Appendix (producer reply, 2026-11-21) plus the brief's AC1–AC7,
  *Key Files* and *Risks and assumptions* sections, which the slices restate rather than reinterpret.

# Tests: origin/trade intel, defusal rule, record and report (red-first)

Red-first test gate for the **pure core** of the pre-emptive counter-push
(parent AH-0MWL7P5T50030229). Written **before** any production change and
failing on `dev` today; turned green by the intel, tick and report children.

## Why this is first

The defusal rule is arithmetic over stored numbers and must stay replayable
(AC4, AC8). Every behaviour is pinned here before a line of production code
changes, so the byte-identical regression gate and the seeded-draw order are
proven by construction rather than asserted afterwards.

## Scope

Pin, in `src/core/hangarWar/`:

1. **The published origin.** `HexPendingAttackIntel` gains `originId` and
   `originAggression`, derived by the shipped `attackingNeighbour(target,
   payload.ring.hexes)` on the **stored pre-redistribution** payload with **no**
   origin exclusion (the fairness exclusion would hide the very origin being
   defused — parent Q3 = A, Q2 = A). Pin `null` when the target has no unheld
   neighbour.
2. **The trade panel.** The `PENDING ATTACK` content published for the map
   names the origin, its aggression, the force, the defender rating, the margin
   and the held hex at risk — all read from the model, none re-derived in a
   scene.
3. **Defusal on a win.** A winning deployment (`deploymentWon: true`) whose
   target hex is the natural pre-redistribution origin of a queued attack
   cancels that attack: no `HexDefenceRecord` for the attacked hex, its defence
   is not resolved on that tick, `pendingAttacks` is cleared, and a defusal entry
   is recorded on `FrontierTickRecord`.
4. **No defusal on a loss.** `deploymentWon: false` at the same origin resolves
   exactly as today, including the sibling fair-origin re-origination
   (AH-0MWH3A87Z005LLOX) and the ordinary skill/`resolveDefence` path.
5. **Byte-identical no-change regression.** With no queued attack (or no
   `deploymentWon`/`playerAttackingHexId`), the tick's payload, clock and record
   are deep-equal to the pre-change fixture, and the 70 % attack-chance draw
   consumes and yields exactly the same value and order as today.
6. **Replay determinism.** Identical `(payload, seed, tick, attackingHex,
   deploymentWon)` inputs yield deep-equal results across reruns, and a defusal
   consumes **no** seeded draw (the following draw is unchanged with and without
   the defusal).
7. **The report line.** `DefenceReportModel.defusalLine` is built from the
   record's defusal entries and is `null` for an ordinary report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` pins the origin id and origin aggression derivation (including the `null` no-neighbour case) and the full `PENDING ATTACK` panel content, and asserts the derivation consumes no seeded draw.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts` pins defusal on a win (no record, no defence resolution, attack consumed, defusal entry recorded) and non-defusal on a loss with the fair-origin rule intact.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts` pins the byte-identical no-change regression against a pre-change fixture and the unchanged 70 % attack-chance draw value and order.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts` pins replay determinism for `(payload, seed, tick, attackingHex, deploymentWon)` and that a defusal consumes no seeded draw.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.test.ts` pins `defusalLine` text for a defusal record and `null` for an ordinary record.
- Every test in this item fails on `dev` for the intended reason (missing origin field / no defusal behaviour) and no production file is modified by this item.

- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: Automated tests pin the pre-deployment panel content (origin and trade), defusal on a win, non-defusal on a loss, the no-change regression, both PlayScene tick paths and replay determinism for (payload, seed, tick, attackingHex, deploymentWon).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the existing `hexIntel.test.ts`, `hexDefence.test.ts` and `defenceReport.test.ts` suites; reuse `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts` for the ring payloads.
- Snapshot the pre-change tick output into a local fixture inside the test file so the regression is self-contained.
- No production edits: this item is tests only.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`

## Dependencies

None — this is the first item in the plan.

## Deliverables

Failing (red) tests covering AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC6, AC8 (pure-core half).

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWL7P5T50030229
- Sibling dependency (shipped): AH-0MWH3A87Z005LLOX — the fair-origin rule these tests must not weaken.

# Tests: PlayScene tick paths, gym parity, old-save and docs assertion (red-first)

Red-first test gate for the **integration** half of the pre-emptive counter-push
(parent AH-0MWL7P5T50030229). Written before the production changes in the scene,
gym and docs children, and failing on `dev` today.

## Why this is separate from the pure-core gate

The pure-core item (sibling, created first) pins the arithmetic. This item pins
the two seams that can silently lose the feature: the **live game** must hand the
deployment's outcome to the tick on **both** paths, and the **gym** must exercise
the same shipped code so gym↔game parity cannot drift
(`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, project convention).

## Scope

1. **Both `PlayScene` tick paths.** `_resolveBetweenSortieTick` receives the
   deployment outcome and passes it as `deploymentWon` on the mini-boss victory
   path (`true`) and the run-end handoff path (`false`), while still passing
   `playerAttackingHexId`. The reused `pendingBetweenSortieTick` is not
   re-resolved on the loss path.
2. **No scene-local arithmetic.** The scene passes inputs only; the defusal
   decision stays inside the pure tick (AC5).
3. **Gym parity surface.** `GymHexWar` can queue an attack, declare the attacking
   hex and the win/loss outcome, and show both the pre-deployment threat panel
   and the defusal outcome through `runFrontierTick` → `buildHexMapModel` →
   `renderHexMap`, with no gym-local copy of the rule or the numbers.
4. **Old-save compatibility.** A payload written before this change (no new
   persisted field) loads and resolves exactly as today.
5. **Docs assertion.** The `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` `GymHexWar` row names the origin
   panel and the defusal rule for this item. That assertion lives with the
   documentation child (which adds `src/counterPushDocs.test.ts`) rather than
   here, so this item stays behavioural.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `PlayScene` hangar-war test pins that the winning path calls the tick with `deploymentWon: true` and the losing path with `deploymentWon: false`, both carrying the deployment's `hexId`, and that no defusal arithmetic exists in the scene.
- A `PlayScene` test pins that a win-reused `pendingBetweenSortieTick` is not re-resolved on the run-end handoff.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` pins queue → declare origin → `tick(win)` defusal and the non-defusal on a loss, with the threat panel and defusal line rendered from the shipped model.
- A payload captured before this change loads and resolves byte-identically (no new persisted field, no schema bump).
- Every test in this item fails on `dev` for the intended reason and no production file is modified by this item.

- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: Both PlayScene tick paths carry the deployment hexId and its outcome, winning path at the mini-boss victory and losing path at the run-end handoff, and the defusal arithmetic is decided inside the pure tick, never in PlayScene.
- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: No new persisted field: the decision inputs are the existing HangarWarDeployment hexId, the existing pendingAttacks and the transient win/loss outcome; the queued attack origin is derived by attackingNeighbour on the stored payload before this tick redistribution, so a save written before this change loads and resolves exactly as today.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/scenes/PlayScene.hangarWar.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`.
- Reuse the shipped harness double (`src/core/hangarWar/fakeFrontierClock.ts`) for deterministic gym ticks.
- No production edits: this item is tests only.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.hangarWar.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None at test-authoring time (the assertions are expected to fail); the
implementation children depend on this item.

## Deliverables

Failing (red) tests covering AC5, AC6, AC7 and AC8 (integration half).

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWL7P5T50030229
- Pure-core test gate: the sibling red-first item created immediately before this one.

# Publish the pending attack's origin and the strike-or-hold trade

The first user-visible slice of the pre-emptive counter-push
(AH-0MWL7P5T50030229): the hex map's pre-deployment threat panel stops saying
only "something is coming and here is the arithmetic" and starts saying **where
it is coming from**, so the player has a hex to strike.

## Target outcome

A player looking at a hex with a queued attack sees, before deploying, the
attacking origin's id and aggression alongside the shipped force / defender
rating / margin, and can weigh **strike first** against **reinforce and hold**
over the same salvage.

## Scope

- `HexPendingAttackIntel` gains the derived origin: `originId` and
  `originAggression`.
- The origin is derived by the **shipped** `attackingNeighbour(target,
  payload.ring.hexes)` on the **stored pre-redistribution** payload, with **no**
  origin exclusion (parent Q3 = A). No new persisted field, no schema bump.
- The `PENDING ATTACK` panel content published for the map states the trade: the
  origin and its aggression, the target's force, the defender rating (with
  upgrade contribution where already published), the margin, and the fact that
  the named hex is the one at risk.

  shipped origin helper. No scene-local arithmetic and no second copy of the

- The `PENDING ATTACK` panel content names the origin id and its aggression alongside the existing force, defender rating and margin, and names the held hex at risk.
- The derivation is additive: every existing `hexIntel` test passes unchanged and no persisted payload field is added.
- The build is pure — the intel derivation consumes no seeded draw and is deterministic for a fixed payload.
- The `hexIntel.ts` docblock that currently says a queued attack "carries a force but no origin" is rewritten to describe the published origin and names AH-0MWL7P5T50030229.

- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: The hex map publishes a queued attack before deployment with its origin: HexPendingAttackIntel gains the attacking origin id and its aggression, derived by the shipped attackingNeighbour on the stored pre-redistribution payload, and the panel states the trade with the previewDefence numbers, no scene-local arithmetic and the held hex that stands to be hit.

# Defusal rule in the pure frontier tick

The engine slice of the pre-emptive counter-push (AH-0MWL7P5T50030229): a
**winning** deployment at the origin of a queued attack cancels that attack
inside the pure tick, and is recorded so the report can announce it.

## Target outcome

Striking first is mechanically real. Win at the hex that is about to hit you and
the queued attack never lands; lose and it resolves exactly as it does today.

## Scope

- `FrontierTickOptions` gains `deploymentWon?: boolean` (default `false` =
  today's behaviour), documented as a **transient** input derived from the
  deployment — never persisted (parent Q4 assumption, AC6 holds).
- In the pending-attack loop, each queued attack's **natural** pre-redistribution
  origin is derived from the **input** `payload` (not the redistributed `next`)
  and with **no** origin exclusion, so the check asks "would this attack have
  originated at the hex I am attacking?" (parent Q3 = A).
- When `deploymentWon === true` and that origin equals `playerAttackingHexId`,
  the attack is cancelled: skip `resolveAttack`/`applyDefence` for it and record a
  defusal entry (attacked hex id, origin id, force) on `FrontierTickRecord`.
- Defusal wins over the sibling fair-origin fallback (parent Q2 = A): a defused
  attack is cancelled outright and never re-originates from another unheld
  neighbour, so the announcement is literally true.
- A loss (or any other case) resolves exactly as today, fair-origin rule intact.
- The defusal check is pure arithmetic and consumes **no** seeded draw.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `FrontierTickOptions.deploymentWon?: boolean` exists, defaults to `false`, and is documented in `hexDefence.ts` as transient (no payload field, no schema version bump).
- On a win whose deployment hex is a queued attack's natural pre-redistribution origin, that attack produces no `HexDefenceRecord`, the target's defence is not resolved on that tick, and `pendingAttacks` is consumed as today.
- The cancelled attack is recorded on `FrontierTickRecord` (attacked hex, origin id, force) so no surface re-derives it; the field is additive and absent/empty for an ordinary tick.
- On a loss at the same origin the tick resolves exactly as today, including re-origination from the next most aggressive unheld neighbour.
- With `deploymentWon` omitted or `false` the tick's payload, clock and record are deep-equal to the pre-change behaviour, and the 70 % attack-chance draw order and value are unchanged.
- A defusal consumes no seeded draw: replaying `(payload, seed, tick, attackingHex, deploymentWon)` yields deep-equal results, and the draw after a defusal equals the draw without it.
- Every existing `resolveDefence` and `runFrontierTick` test passes unchanged.

- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: A winning deployment whose target hex is the origin of a queued attack cancels that attack in the same payload write: the target hex defence is not resolved on that tick, and the rolled-in defence report announces the defusal.
- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: A losing deployment at that origin leaves the queued attack intact and it resolves exactly as today, including the sibling fair-origin rule.
- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: An ordinary deployment with no queued attack at its origin is byte-identical to today's tick: the existing resolveDefence, attackingNeighbour and runFrontierTick suites pass unchanged and the 70% attack-chance draw order is unchanged.
- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: No new persisted field: the queued attack origin is derived by attackingNeighbour on the stored payload before this tick redistribution, so a save written before this change loads and resolves exactly as today.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the option beside the shipped `playerAttackingHexId` and normalise it to a boolean with a `false` default.
- Derive the natural origin once per queued attack from the input payload via the shipped `attackingNeighbour` with no exclusion list, then branch before `resolveAttack`.
- Accumulate defusal entries in a local array and attach them to the record.
- Extend the existing pending-attack loop; do not restructure the redistribution or the 70 % draw path.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the pure-core red-first test gate (sibling item created before this one).

## Deliverables

The defusal rule in the pure, replayable tick with its record, pinned by tests.

## Notes

- `types.ts` needs **no** schema change; confirm only (AC6).
- Accepted caveat from intake Q3: the pre-redistribution origin can differ from
  the origin the resolver would have used after redistribution, so a defusal may
  name an origin today's resolver would not have attacked from. Accepted by the
  producer; record it in the code comment beside the rule.

# Announce the defusal in the rolled-in defence report

The announcement slice of the pre-emptive counter-push (AH-0MWL7P5T50030229): a
defused attack is reported, not silently dropped, so the player sees that
striking first worked.

## Target outcome

The post-sortie map reads "_struck first at hex X — the attack on hex Y never
launched_" instead of an unexplained absence of the attack the player was warned
about.

- `DefenceReportModel` gains `defusalLine: string | null`, built from the tick

# Thread the deployment outcome through both PlayScene tick paths

The live-game wiring slice of the pre-emptive counter-push
(AH-0MWL7P5T50030229): the between-sortie tick learns whether the sortie was won
or lost, on both paths, without any arithmetic leaving the pure tick.

## Target outcome

In a real run, winning at the hex that was about to attack you defuses the queued
attack; losing there lets it land. The behaviour the gym demonstrates is the
behaviour the game runs.

## Scope

- `_resolveBetweenSortieTick(won: boolean)` gains the outcome and passes
  `deploymentWon: won` alongside the shipped `playerAttackingHexId`.
- The mini-boss victory path (`_finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory`, which resolves
  the tick before the capture) passes `true`.
- The run-end handoff (`_finishRun`, which resolves the tick on a loss) passes
  `false`.
- The already-resolved `pendingBetweenSortieTick` is reused on the loss path after
  a win — not re-resolved.
- The scene passes inputs only: the defusal decision stays in `runFrontierTick`
  (AC5).

- `_resolveBetweenSortieTick` accepts the deployment outcome and forwards it as `deploymentWon` together with the deployment's `hexId` as `playerAttackingHexId`.
- The mini-boss victory path calls the tick with `deploymentWon: true`; the run-end loss path calls it with `deploymentWon: false`.
- A win-resolved `pendingBetweenSortieTick` is reused at run end and the tick is not resolved twice.
- No defusal, origin or rating arithmetic exists in `PlayScene.ts`; the scene only forwards the outcome.
- The existing `PlayScene` hangar-war suites pass unchanged, and the new path assertions are green.

- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: Both PlayScene tick paths carry the deployment hexId and its outcome, winning path at the mini-boss victory and losing path at the run-end handoff, and the defusal arithmetic is decided inside the pure tick, never in PlayScene.

## Minimal Implementation

# GymHexWar parity surface for the counter-push

The parity slice of the pre-emptive counter-push (AH-0MWL7P5T50030229): the gym
can queue an attack, declare the attacking hex and the deployment outcome, and
shows both the pre-deployment threat panel and the defusal outcome through the
**shipped** code path — so the rule can never drift between gym and game.

## Target outcome

A someone can demonstrate and verify the whole mechanic without a browser run:
queue → see the origin on the map → declare the strike → tick(win) → read the
defusal in the report.

## Scope

- `GymHexWar` control surfaces gain what is needed to (a) queue an attack,
  (b) declare the attacking hex (already shipped as `setPlayerAttackingHex`),
  (c) declare the deployment outcome, and (d) tick.
- The pre-deployment threat panel and the defusal outcome are rendered by the
  shared `buildHexMapModel` / `renderHexMap` pair — no gym-local copy of the
  origin derivation, the defusal decision or the report line.
- The `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` `GymHexWar` row records the origin panel and the
  defusal rule, naming this item.
- The scene keeps its documented read-only, no-handler character: no new
  actionable rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GymHexWar` can queue a pending attack, declare the attacking hex and declare a winning tick, and the rendered map shows the threat panel with the origin and the defusal line — all through `runFrontierTick` → `buildHexMapModel` → `renderHexMap`.
- A losing tick at the same origin shows the attack resolving with no defusal line, matching the game's behaviour.
- The gym owns no origin derivation, defusal decision or report wording; every number and line comes from the shipped modules.
- The `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` `GymHexWar` row names the origin panel, the defusal rule and AH-0MWL7P5T50030229, and the parity-assertion test passes.
- The gym remains read-only: `isUpgradeVisible()` stays `false` and no test asserts a new actionable row.

- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: GymHexWar can queue an attack, declare the attacking hex and show both the pre-deployment threat panel and the defusal outcome through the shipped code path, with the row in docs/GYM_PARITY.md updated.

## Problem statement

The gym power-up placement keeps a new drop clear of the ship by the *icon*
radius (`POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` = 16 px), but the shared pickup gate collects on
the ship's hull plus the drop's **aura bubble** radius
(`dropBubbleRadius(16) × scale` = 22.4 px at full scale). The two do not match:

- placement clearance: `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` = 16 px (strict `<`, so ≥ 26 px is "clear");
- pickup radius at full scale: `dropBubbleRadius(16) × 1 = 22.4 px` (`<=`).

A drop placed in the 16–22.4 px annulus is therefore **already inside the
pickup bubble** at full scale and is collected without the player flying into
it — as soon as its grow animation (0.5 s) passes the matching scale.

Found while fixing a flaky test (AH-0MWRTPX0V007MXY6): the gym's boot-placed
drop could mature mid-window and be collected by the stationary ship, which
resets the shared Mining Laser cadence timer and fabricated an extra shot.

## Users

- **Gym-level designers**: drops placed during gym boot-up must not be
  instantly collectible.
- **Game players**: drops should require intentional approach, not spawn in the
  ship's lap.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `GymFormationScene._powerUpPlacementContext()` and `GymLevel._supplyPlacementContext()` pass `dropBubbleRadius(POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE)` as `dropRadius`, so a placed drop is never instantly collectible.
2. A unit test pins the invariant: for a full-scale drop, the placement clearance is greater than or equal to the shared collection radius (`dropCollectRadius(POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE, 1)`).
3. The gym suites (`GymMinerals`, `GymLevel`, power-up gyms) stay green.
4. `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` notes the corrected clearance where relevant (or the placement doc comment states the pickup-radius basis).

## Impact

Gym power-up drops no longer spawn inside the ship's pickup bubble, eliminating spurious instant pickups and the cadence-timer resets they caused during gym boot-up.

## Constraints

- `PlayScene` does not use `RandomAvoidingPlacement` (its drops spawn at the
  kill site), so this is a gym-only surface.
- Behaviour change is small and player-favourable: drops never spawn in the
  ship's lap.
- The flaky test is already guarded test-side by `clearFieldDrops`
  (AH-0MWRTPX0V007MXY6), so this item is not blocking.

## Existing state

- `_powerUpPlacementContext()` (GymFormationScene.ts:1107) uses `dropRadius: POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` (16 px).
- `_supplyPlacementContext()` (GymLevel.ts:1644) uses `dropRadius: POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` (16 px).
- `dropBubbleRadius()` returns `size × 1.4` = 22.4 px for a 16 px drop.
- `dropCollectRadius()` = `dropBubbleRadius() × scale`.

## Desired change

Replace `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` with `dropBubbleRadius(POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE)` in both placement context methods.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_powerUpPlacementContext()`, change `dropRadius: POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` to `dropRadius: dropBubbleRadius(POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE)`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — `_supplyPlacementContext()`, change `dropRadius: POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` to `dropRadius: dropBubbleRadius(POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE)`
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — `dropBubbleRadius()` (read-only reference)
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — update clearance notes

## Related work

- **Discovered-from:** AH-0MWRTPX0V007MXY6 — flaky GymMinerals cadence test
- **Collection radius parity:** AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4 — collection matches the bubble

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were raised — the item was sufficiently defined from
the work-item description.

# Close the one-level mineral income gap that collection cannot recover

## Problem statement

The collection re-tune (parent AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J) can raise **collected ÷ spawned** salvage toward its ceiling but **cannot reach the pre-pass-through target of 9.0 (ring 1) / 6.0 (ring 2) minerals/deployment** — a read-only spike on `63f82a791` measured the perfect-collection ceiling at only **7.67 / 5.53**. That item's AC1 explicitly left open the possibility that "the fix may be **harness fidelity**, not a game balance change — investigate before touching drop rates".

**The investigation is now done, and it confirms the harness-fidelity hypothesis.** The headless arena the income measurement is derived from does **not model the game's mineral economy at all**:

- **The arena** seeds a **static mineral field** of `spawns.minerals × 3 = 18` points (`DEFAULT_ARENA_SPAWNS.minerals = 6`), tops the field back up to 6 every 150 ticks from that same 18-point reservoir, and **never drops a mineral on a kill** (it drops power-ups via the real per-kill rule in campaign mode, but not minerals). So the arena's total per-sortie mineral supply is a hard-coded **18**, unrelated to enemy count or player performance.
- **The shipped game** seeds **no mineral field at all** (`PlayScene.resetRunState` clears `this.minerals = []`; the only procedural mineral spawner, `spawnMineralAt`, has *zero* non-test callers). The game's minerals come **entirely from enemy kill drops** through the shared `resolveMineralKillPayout` rule — `2 × round(collected + bonus[0.25–1.25])` per non-asteroid kill, plus 2 per small asteroid (GDD §4.4.1). That is **≈1.5 minerals per non-asteroid kill**, so a level-1 five-wave sortie (42 enemies) supplies **≈63 minerals from kills** — roughly **3.5×** what the arena offers, before enemy mineral absorption inflates the re-drop count further.

So the arena's "perfect collection" ceiling of 7.67 / 5.53 is an **artefact of the harness's 18-mineral field**, not a property of the shipped game's economy. The gap the collection item could not recover is very likely a **measurement-fidelity gap**, not a real balance shortfall.

## Desired outcome

Close the residual gap between the measured perfect-collection ceiling (7.67 / 5.53) and the pre-pass-through baseline (9.0 / 6.0) by **restoring the arena's mineral fidelity to the shipped game, then re-measuring** — before any game balance change is considered:

1. **Confirm and quantify the divergence** between the arena's mineral supply and the shipped game's per-sortie mineral availability (the arena's static 18-field vs the game's kill-drop economy), recording both the mechanism and the measured per-sortie figures.
2. **Fix the fidelity gap** in the arena's mineral supply so the measured per-deployment income reflects the game the unlock tree was balanced against — modelling the game's real mineral kill-drop/absorption economy (or, if a full model is out of scope, calibrating the arena's mineral supply to the measured game-equivalent per-sortie availability), then re-measure ring-1/ring-2 income.
3. **If the gap still does not close** after the fidelity fix, decide between an economy-side change to the **game** (spawn/drop rate or capture rate) and recording the achievable ceiling as the accepted balance point — with the measurement as the evidence either way.

## Users

- **Hangar War players** — per-deployment mineral income is the pace at which the unlock tree (hulls, weapons, modifiers) is bought between sorties; a lower income is felt directly as a longer grind.
- **The designer/producer** — owns the trade between the measurement harness's fidelity and the design targets built on it. A harness that under-supplies minerals invalidates every income-derived balance conclusion.

Example user story: *As a Hangar War player, I want my between-sortie income to reflect the field the unlock tree was actually balanced against — so a sortie that looks mineral-rich pays like one, rather than being capped by a harness constant.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- The **arena's per-sortie mineral availability is measured against the shipped game** — the mechanism (static 18-field with no kill-drops vs the game's kill-drop-only economy) and the per-sortie figure at each ring's aggression-selected level are both recorded with the command that reproduces them.
- **The arena's mineral supply is made faithful to the shipped game** so a measured run's mineral supply tracks the game's real kill-drop/absorption economy rather than a fixed 18-point field (modelling the game rule, or calibrating the arena supply to the measured game-equivalent availability if a full model is out of scope), with the chosen approach and its justification recorded.
- **Re-measured income** (seeds 1–3, competent bot, shipped five-wave sortie) is recorded for both rings, and either **moves ring-1/ring-2 minerals/deployment toward 9.0 / 6.0** or records the achievable ceiling as the accepted balance point with the reason.
- Any further economy-side change (game spawn/drop rate or capture rate) is only considered **after** the fidelity fix and is backed by its own measurement; collection routing is **not** changed here (owned by AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J).
- The committed income artifact `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json`, the income guard in `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, and GDD §8.2 *Measured per-deployment income (one-level sortie)* are re-pinned to the resulting measurement, with the reason for each changed pin recorded in a comment.
- A deterministic guard fails if the committed income artifact diverges from a fresh measurement of the shipped bot (or the arena's mineral model diverges from its documented game-faithful contract).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (if it quotes these figures) and the GDD.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player's between-sortie income reflects a field that actually pays the minerals the unlock tree was balanced against, rather than a sortie that cannot spawn enough salvage for collection to matter.

## Constraints

- **No change to collection routing** — that is owned by AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J. This item is the arena/economy side only.
- **Balance figures are measured, not guessed** — use the ring-timing harness; the artifact is the evidence.
- **Arena changes are shared infrastructure** — the headless arena feeds aim, churn, ring-timing and income measurements. Any mineral-model change re-baselines those derived figures and must be re-pinned deliberately, not silently.
- **Determinism preserved** — arena changes must keep same-policy + same-config + same-seed ⇒ byte-identical records (no wall-clock reads, every draw from a seeded stream).
- Prefer modelling the **real game rule** over inventing a new harness constant; a game balance change to compensate for a harness artefact would bake the artefact in.

## Existing state

- **The arena's mineral model** (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`): `mineralReservoir` of `spawns.minerals × 3` (= 18) points at line 963–964; `nextMineral` only decrements (line 1632–1641), so the reservoir is a **hard per-run cap**; replenish tops the field back to 6 every `COLLECTABLE_RESPAWN_TICKS` (150) from the same reservoir (line 2418–2422). In campaign/per-level mode `realSupplyMode` swaps the **power-up** supply to the real per-kill rule but leaves minerals on the static field (line 1877–1891 pushes only `world.drops`, never `world.minerals`).
- **The shipped game's mineral model** (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`): `resetRunState` sets `this.minerals = []` (line 1734) — no seeded field; the only non-test mineral source is `resolveMineralKillPayout` on kill (line 5254–5258), the shared rule in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`; `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount` (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:682`) is `MINERAL_DROP_MULTIPLIER (2) × round(collected + bonus[0.25–1.25])`. `spawnMineralAt` (line 6309) has no production callers.
- **Measured baseline** (parent's spike on `63f82a791`): perfect-collection ceiling **7.67 (ring 1) / 5.53 (ring 2)** minerals/deployment; captured sorties bank **16.75 / 8.0** at the mini-boss checkpoint; capture rates **50 % / 50 %**.
- **The committed income artifact** `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` records 7.44 / 2.67 at 44.4 % / 33.3 % (stale by many commits); the ring-timing guard pins `mineralsPerCapturedDeployment ≈ 16.75` and the ring-1/ring-2 unlock pace.

## Desired change

Make the arena's mineral supply model the shipped game's mineral economy (kill-drops from the shared rule, with the real absorption/re-drop behaviour) — or, if a full model is too broad for this item, calibrate the arena's mineral supply to the measured game-equivalent per-sortie availability — then re-measure ring-1/ring-2 income, re-pin the artifact/guards/GDD, and record whether the 9.0 / 6.0 target is reached or the achievable ceiling is the accepted balance point.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the mineral reservoir, replenish cadence and the kill seam (`destroyHostile`) where a faithful mineral kill-drop/absorption model would live.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — `DEFAULT_ARENA_SPAWNS` / `ArenaSpawns` if the mineral supply becomes configurable or is re-documented.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — the shared game kill-drop rule the arena should consume (single source of truth).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `mineralRedropCount` / `collectMineral` (the absorption → re-drop behaviour to mirror).
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — regenerate from the re-measured income.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — re-pin the income and unlock-pace guards; add a fidelity guard if appropriate.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2 *Measured per-deployment income (one-level sortie)* table, verdict and pace figures.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` / `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — the arena's documented fidelity boundaries (they currently state the seeded mineral harvest stays live).
- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs` — the regeneration CLI (`--one-level --income-out`).

## Related work

- **AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J** — Review the per-deployment mineral income after pass-through collection (parent; its AC1 designated the harness-fidelity path investigated here).
- **AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P** — Implement route-through collection re-tune (sibling; collection routing, out of scope here).
- **AH-0MWLLPAQL003IEXE** — Regenerate income artifact, re-pin guards and update docs (sibling; execution of the re-pin).
- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** — Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment (produced the income artifact + guards).
- **AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB** — the shared mineral kill-drop rule (parent of `mineralKillDrops.ts`).
- **AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT** — Mineral collectable entity and constants.
- **AH-0MUCST1AX00483RX** — Test: Mineral entity lifecycle and collection semantics.
- **AH-0MUX96GJF006CAZP** — Enable mineral collection between waves.
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — the measurement artifact.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — the documented income verdict and pace table.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the arena's documented fidelity boundaries.
- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs` — the regeneration CLI.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — re-baselining the shared arena.** The arena feeds aim, churn, ring-timing and income measurements; changing its mineral model re-baselines all of them. Mitigation: keep the change behind the campaign/one-level supply path where possible, re-pin each affected guard deliberately with a reason, and record the before/after measurement.
- **Risk — modelling absorption is broad.** Mirroring the game's absorb→re-drop behaviour needs enemies to collect minerals in the arena, which the current stationary-hostile model does not do. Mitigation: prefer the real kill-drop rule first; if full absorption modelling is out of scope, calibrate the arena supply to the measured game-equivalent availability and document the remaining approximation under the arena's existing *fidelity boundary* convention.
- **Risk — the gap may not fully close.** Even with faithful availability the bot may collect less than the game ceiling; the item's ACs allow recording the achievable ceiling as the accepted balance point, so the target is never silently restated.
- **Assumption — the pre-pass-through 9.0 / 6.0 figures are the target** because they are what the GDD and unlock-pace table were baselined on; if the fidelity fix shows they were themselves measured on the unfaithful arena, the re-measured game-faithful figures become the new reference and the unlock pace is re-derived from them.
- **Assumption — small evidence set.** Seeds 1–3 can make a capture-rate move of a deployment or two read as variance; a capture-rate conclusion should be confirmed on a wider seed set.
- **Scope-creep risk:** changing hangar prices, drop rates or the unlock tree is a separate balance item with its own measurement, not something to absorb here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q — Harness fidelity vs game balance (open question raised by this investigation).** The investigation shows the arena under-supplies minerals (static 18-field, no kill-drops) relative to the shipped game (~63 from kills on a level-1 sortie), so the "perfect-collection ceiling" may be a harness artefact. Should the fix be (a) make the arena model the game's real mineral kill-drop/absorption economy and re-measure, (b) calibrate the arena's mineral supply to the measured game-equivalent availability (smaller change), or (c) record the current arena ceiling as the accepted balance point? **OPEN QUESTION** — this item's AC1 pre-authorised the harness-fidelity investigation ("the fix may be harness fidelity, not a game balance change"), so intake proceeds on path (a)/(b); the producer should confirm the approach at review. **Recommended:** (a) if feasible, else (b) — either restores fidelity; (c) only if the producer judges the arena's static model an acceptable proxy. Source: repo investigation (see Evidence below).
  - **Evidence (research).** `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`: `mineralReservoir` = `spawns.minerals × 3 = 18` (963–964), `nextMineral` only decrements (1632–1641), replenish from the same reservoir every 150 ticks (2418–2422), and `realSupplyMode` drops only power-ups on kill (1877–1891). `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`: `this.minerals = []` on reset (1734), minerals only from `resolveMineralKillPayout` on kill (5254–5258), `spawnMineralAt` has no production callers. `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:682`: `mineralRedropCount = 2 × round(collected + bonus[0.25–1.25])` ⇒ ≈1.5 minerals per non-asteroid kill. Level-1 five-wave sortie = 42 enemies ⇒ ≈63 minerals from kills.
- **Q — Where does the 9.0 / 6.0 target come from?** — It is the pre-pass-through one-level income measurement the GDD and unlock-pace table were baselined on (parent AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J). **Assumption recorded:** if the fidelity fix re-measures new game-faithful figures, those become the reference and the unlock pace is re-derived from them (the parent AC's documented fallback). Source: parent item description.
